LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights How to watch as these two teams take center stage on "Thursday Night Football" after Week 7 losses IMAGN Images via Reuters Connect In the Week 8 edition of "Thursday Night Football," the Green Bay Packers play host to the Carolina Panthers . The Packers enter this game off a disappointing loss to the division rival Detroit Lions , in a game they had multiple chances to win. Green Bay had won three in a row to salvage its season after a blowout loss to the Atlanta Falcons the last time the Packers played on Thursday night (Week 3), but they hit a bump in the road last week. Now, they're looking to make it four wins in five games. The Panthers are coming off an embarrassing blowout loss at the hands of the division rival Tampa Bay Buccaneers . Carolina was blasted 43-13 last week and was never truly competitive, falling down 17-0 early. However, the Panthers still sit at .500 after climbing that hump with their win over the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 6. Now, they try to get back to their winning ways. Which of these two teams will get back in the win column? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game. Where to watch Packers vs. Panthers live Date: Thursday, Oct. 29 | Time: 8:20 p.m. ET Location: Lambeau Field (Green Bay) Streaming: Amazon Prime Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Packers -3/5, O/U 47.5 via DraftKings Sportsbook When the Panthers have the ball The Panthers limped to their worst offensive performance of the season last week, managing just 266 yards, 15 first downs and 13 points while turning the ball over four times. They had previously gained at least 340 yards in every game, gained at least 24 first downs in four of five, and scored 25-plus points in four of five. Bryce Young returned to poor form on Sunday, going only 14-of-27 for 163 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions, while also fumbling once. He's now completed south of 52% of his passes in back-to-back games and south of 55% in three of his last four, with the only exception being a game against the decrepit Lions pass defense. Young got off to a hot start to the season , but he's cooled off a bit as of late. The Packers have been a tough matchup for opposing quarterbacks this year. They're eighth in net passing yards per attempt, and they've yet to allow more than 296 net passing yards in any game this season. They've also allowed just nine touchdown passes against nine interceptions. Jonathan Gannon has been good at limiting what opponents can do through the air, for the most part. It is, however, worth noting that the Packers faced Carson Wentz , Geno Smith , Michael Penix Jr. , Jalon Daniels and Tyson Bagent before getting Dak Prescott and Jared Goff over the last two weeks. So they haven't exactly done this against a murderer's row of opponents. Green Bay has gotten pressure at a below-average rate — no surprise with Micah Parsons still sidelined. Instead, the Packers have gotten by against the pass with sticky coverage and timely plays on the ball. Keisean Nixon and Brandon Cisse have been solid on the outside. Javon Bullard has played well in the slot, and the safeties are providing quality help over the top and in the middle of the field. Carolina's passing game is mostly built outside the numbers with Tetairoa McMillan and Jalen Coker , though Young has thrown over the middle more this season than in past years. It'll be up to the skyscrapers on the perimeter to win their one-on-one matchups here in order to give Young room to throw, though he should have more time than he did last week thanks to Green Bay's relatively weaker pass rush. In the run game, the Panthers lean on Chuba Hubbard , who is averaging 4.8 yards per carry in a workhorse role in the absence of Jonathon Brooks . Hubbard only got seven carries in the negative game script last week, but you can likely expect the Panthers to try to "Establish The Run" here as a way to get their offense back on track. Green Bay has allowed only 3.9 yards per carry this season, though, so it might be tough, especially with right tackle Taylor Moton now on the sidelines. When the Packers have the ball The Packers welcomed Josh Jacobs back to the lineup last week but still found themselves entirely unable to run the ball against the Lions. They totaled just 60 yards on the ground, with Jacobs himself carrying 11 times for only 36 yards. Green Bay is now averaging a pathetic 2.9 yards per carry on the season, which unsurprisingly ranks dead last in the league. The Panthers, meanwhile, were run over by the Bucs last week. Bucky Irving and Co. blew past Carolina for a remarkable 258 yards on the ground, which was made all the more incredible by the fact that the Panthers had yielded just 81 rushing yards in their previous two games combined. Still, Carolina has allowed 5.2 yards per carry on the season now, which, to no surprise, ranks dead last. Almost 60% of the rushing yards the Panthers have allowed, though, came in their games against the Bucs and the Chicago Bears in Week 1. They've been fine-ish against the run otherwise. So, can the Packers run the ball with any degree of success here? If the recent history of this season is any indication, then the answer is probably not. Jacobs has been at or below 4.0 yards per carry in two of his last three full seasons, and spending six weeks on the commissioner's exempt list in the wake of a disturbing domestic violence incident probably didn't make him a more efficient runner. And the offensive line is still not a good run-blocking unit. So, the fate of the Packers' offense likely once again falls on the right shoulder of Jordan Love . Love has only completed 59.8% of his passes at an average of 7.4 yards per attempt this season, but he's been victimized by a league-high 21 drops, according to Tru Media. Love is attacking deep downfield consistently, with a 9.1-yard average depth of throw that ranks fourth-highest in the NFL . As such, he's created explosive plays (16-plus-yard gains) at the third-highest rate in the league among 33 qualified quarterbacks. He should see favorable matchups when he looks downfield on Thursday night. Panthers starting cornerbacks Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson remain out on injured reserve, which has left rookie Will Lee III and Akayleb Evans as the starting corners. But Evans is also out on Thursday night, meaning, well, I honestly don't even know who is going to step up in his absence. The Panthers elevated Marco Wilson from the practice squad, and they may need to shift Chau Smith-Wade outside. Either way, it's not a great situation for Carolina. Christian Watson and Matthew Golden , who is trending to play, should be able to find space down the field against these corners, and then it's just a matter of actually hanging onto the ball when Love puts it on them. Green Bay could have a big night through the air if the Packers can protect Love, which will be made easier by the absence of Panthers edge rusher Jaelan Phillips , who is also out for this game. It was surprising to see the Panthers get smacked in the face by the Buccaneers last week. The Packers probably can't do the same thing the Bucs did — run the ball down Carolina's throat — but they can still beat that defense with explosive plays. With the top two cornerbacks still out, Watson and Golden (if he plays) are going to be able to find space in the defense. Green Bay's own defense has also played better as of late after a rough start to the season. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict this weekend's top games Getty Images And then, there was one. The Minnesota Vikings are the only remaining undefeated team in the NFL, as the San Francisco 49ers were handed their first loss by the Atlanta Falcons , while the Kansas City Chiefs took their first "L" to the Seattle Seahawks . The Vikings have a massive matchup this week, as they take on the high-flying Lions in Detroit. Elsewhere around the NFL , Lamar Jackson looks to make his return to the field against Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills , the Cleveland Browns and Pittsburgh Steelers face off for the second time in the last month, and the Chicago Bears travel out west to play Sam Darnold and the Seahawks. Which teams should you pick in Week 8, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Oct. 27 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. Credit to CBS Sports Research Carolina Panthers at Green Bay Packers (-3.5) (TNF) Dajani ( Packers -3.5): I'm willing to overlook the Carolina Panthers ' surprising 43-13 loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . They are a better team than what they showed last Sunday, but it's difficult to overlook the fact that Carolina's rushing defense ranks dead last in the NFL with 153.2 yards allowed per game. Josh Jacobs rushed for just 36 yards on 11 carries last week against the Lions in his 2026 debut, but I think he's in for a massive homecoming in primetime on a short week. I'm not saying the Packers run away with this one, but I'll take them to cover 3.5 points. … Prediction: Packers 27, Panthers 23 Dubin (Packers -3.5): It was surprising to see the Panthers get smacked in the face by the Buccaneers last week. The Packers probably can't do the same thing the Bucs did — run the ball down Carolina's throat — but they can still beat that defense with explosive plays. With the top two cornerbacks still out, Christian Watson and Matthew Golden (if he plays) are going to be able to find space in the defense. Green Bay's own defense has also played better of late after a rough start to the season. … Prediction: Packers 24, Panthers 17 Baltimore Ravens at Buffalo Bills (-3.5) Dajani ( Ravens +3.5): Ignore that Baltimore allowed 35 unanswered points to the Cincinnati Bengals last week, because it appears that Lamar Jackson is back! He was playing some legitimate MVP-level ball before getting hurt, as Jackson went 3-1 as the starter, while completing 70.8% of his passes with 10.1 yards per attempt, six passing touchdowns and just one interception. Only four quarterbacks have put up those kinds of numbers in their first four starts of a season in the past 40 years. The Ravens are a completely different team with Jackson under center, and this Bills defense allows too many points. Buffalo ranks third-worst in scoring defense (28.5 ppg), and has allowed at least 30 points in four of its five victories this season. Jackson is 10-5 SU and 13-2 ATS as an underdog in his career. He's statistically the best quarterback to bet on when listed as an underdog since 1970. … Prediction: Ravens 30, Bills 28 Dubin (Ravens +3.5): This is the same deal as with the Ravens and me pretty much every week: flip the pick if Lamar Jackson sits out again. Otherwise, I like the Ravens to at least keep things close against the Bills. Both of these offenses have been pretty excellent, and the Ravens have been especially so when Jackson has been on the field with Zay Flowers . Ultimately, though, the Bills' home-field advantage and the weaknesses in Baltimore's own pass defense lead me to take the Bills to win and the Ravens to cover. … Prediction: Bills 30, Ravens 27 Minnesota Vikings at Detroit Lions (-3) Dajani (Lions -3): I'm shocked by this line, honestly. The only remaining undefeated team in the NFL is a three-point underdog to a division rival? With that said, I think I agree with it. The Vikings' defense is the main reason they are 5-0, as they've allowed a league-leading 12.3 points per game, plus registered a league-leading 10.6% sack rate and 47.6% pressure rate. Offensively, the Vikings have the fewest touchdowns (10) by a 6-0 team since the 1934 Lions and rank 31st in offensive EPA. They could have lost last week to the Indianapolis Colts , who are in the midst of a fire sale. As for the Lions, the concern has always been with their defense. But I think Kelvin Sheppard 's unit is coming along. They allowed just 17 points to the Packers last week, and Brian Branch is back in the lineup. Maybe we could see a push here, but I'm taking the Lions to win … Prediction: Lions 24, Vikings 20 Dubin (Lions -3): Detroit has recently been thrown off its offensive game by Brian Flores' defense, but the offense is operating at an extremely high level right now, with Jared Goff playing as well as he has in recent memory. And as Dajani said, this Minnesota offense just does not have the ability to get into a high-scoring game and come away with a win. They need the defense to hold the opponent down entirely, and I'm not sure that even Flores' bunch can do that in the friendly confines of Ford Field. … Prediction: Lions 23, Vikings 14 Cleveland Browns at Pittsburgh Steelers (-3.5) Dajani (Steelers -3.5): How can the Browns keep getting away with this? They overcame a 14-0 deficit in Nashville on Sunday, as Harold Fannin Jr . took a short reception 36 yards down the field with 20 seconds remaining to set up a 32-yard game-winning field goal from Andre Szmyt . Deshaun Watson became the third quarterback since 1970 to register a game-winning drive in each of his team's first five wins of the season. With this being a divisional game against an opponent that just got back from Paris, I can understand why some would take the points with the underdog given the hook. But the Steelers are 3-0 ATS at home. That includes Week 3, when they dropped 30 points on Joe Burrow and the Bengals in a win, and Week 5, when Pittsburgh scored 34 points in a double-digit victory over the Colts. The Steelers are averaging 26.0 points per game over their last five contests, which ranks top 10 in the NFL, and are 8-0 SU and ATS in their last eight home games vs. the Browns. In fact, Pittsburgh is actually a perfect 11-0 ATS in its last 11 home divisional games. Insane stat. … Prediction: Steelers 26, Browns 21 Dubin (Steelers -3.5): I don't understand how the Browns keep doing it. Every single one of their victories has required a game-winning drive in the final five minutes of the game. That's not sustainable on any level whatsoever. The Steelers don't exactly have consistency written all over them, considering the vagaries of their passing game and the fact that their three-game winning streak has come against weak opponents. However, I trust Jaylen Warren and Co. more than I do the Browns at this point. … Prediction: Steelers 20, Browns 13 Atlanta Falcons at Tampa Bay Buccaneers (-2.5) Dajani (Falcons +2.5): I have plenty of questions about both of these teams, but I did tell you the Falcons were going to cover the small number vs. the 49ers last week! Atlanta finished that game on a 26-6 run after trailing 14-3. They scored on four straight drives. I'm not sure the Buccaneers deserve to be three-point favorites this week after that destruction of the Panthers. Baker Mayfield had to throw for just 64 yards and a touchdown in a 43-13 victory, as Bucky Irving , Kenneth Gainwell and Sean Tucker combined for 246 yards rushing and three touchdowns. This Falcons rush defense ranks fourth in the NFL with 88.9 rushing yards allowed per game. Plus, the Falcons have won two road games this season by 20+ points after being listed as an underdog, and are 4-0 ATS in their last four road games against the Buccaneers. … Prediction: Falcons 26, Buccaneers 24 Dubin (Falcons +2.5): The Buccaneers ran all over the Panthers last week, but Atlanta has actually been quite good against the run, allowing only 3.8 yards per carry this season. Can Tampa really control the game with Bucky Irving the way it did last week, or will it have to actually turn Baker Mayfield loose as a passer here? If the Bucs have to do that, I have more confidence in Atlanta's offense right now, with Bijan Robinson , Drake London and even Kyle Pitts contributing at a high level. … Prediction: Falcons 23, Buccaneers 17 Kansas City Chiefs (-1.5) at Denver Broncos Dajani ( Broncos +1.5): The Broncos had an embarrassing outing last time they played the Chiefs, allowing 247 yards off of 28 missed tackles in a 31-10 loss. There has been a lot of talk about Bo Nix and the offense, but what about the Chiefs? They averaged 4.3 yards per play and recorded just 213 yards of total offense in that embarrassing loss to the Seahawks. The team seemingly never got off the bus. It was the first game in Andy Reid's head-coaching career in which his team registered zero explosive plays,

Sporting News' Bill Bender is taking the Packers, 27-22. The Packers are coming off a loss against the Detroit Lions in a key NFC North battle in Week 7 and dropped into last place in the division despite a winning record. The Packers won three games in a row after a 1-2 start, and they welcomed back veteran running back Josh Jacobs in Week 7 after he was suspended for the first six games of the campaign. Now, the Packers find themselves as favorites at home against a Carolina team that is just 3-3 in the 2026 season after a blowout loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday. Tampa Bay ran all over Carolina's defense, allowing over five yards per carry this season. And Bryce Young and company are looking to prove that they are an actual playoff contender after winning the division in the 2025 season. Carolina's offense has been pretty good through six games, with Young throwing for a ton of yardage to lead the team to a 3-3 start. But a shaky showing out of the bye in Week 6 certainly puts some pressure on the Panthers as they look to fend off the Atlanta Falcons and the Bucs in the NFC South. Oddsmakers have set the Packers as favorites in this matchup, and Green Bay needs every win it can get to compete in a division where all four teams are currently over .500. Bryce Young, up until last week, had been playing leaps and bounds better than he had the previous three seasons, and I'm of the belief that it's more of a sign of an abnormally strong start against some bad defenses as opposed to a quarterback who improved by tenfold in a single offseason. The Packers' defense ranks 12th in opponent EPA per play and 10th in opponent EPA per dropback, so with them being on their home field on a short week, I expect them to get to Young in this game. I'll take the Packers to cover on Thursday Night Football. Love should be able to attack through the air, as the Panthers are a below-average defense overall (20th in EPA/Play), and they entered Week 7 allowing the most yards per carry in the league. Meanwhile, Green Bay’s defense held a vaunted Detroit offense to just 20 points and is now fifth in the league in EPA/Play. If it weren’t for multiple missed field goals, the Pack could be entering this game with a 5-2 record. The Panthers may end up winning the NFC South, but they are extremely banged up and now have to play on the road in a tough environment on a short week. picks.blurb: Predictions: Will Packers Score Thursday Night Bounce-Back vs. Panthers? It couldn’t possibly go worse than when they lost to the Falcons 35-14 on Thursday night last month. “Yeah, I should change everything, huh?” defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon sort-of joked on Wednesday, “because we laid an egg – me I’m talking about. I hold that to ourselves. I think Matt (LaFleur) made some tweaks, which I really liked. I think it’s going to help our guys. We’ll see, the proof will be in the pudding.” The Packers need to find a victory in the pudding against Carolina. Green Bay is in last place in the NFC North and holds a tenuous grip on the final spot in the NFC. Obviously, it’s early to be overly concerned about the playoff race, but the division race is in danger of getting away from them before the calendar flips to November. Will the Packers win? Here are our weekly predictions. Bill Huber’s Packers-Panthers Prediction The Packers and Panthers are two of the most beat-up teams in the NFL , a fact complicated by playing on a Thursday. The injuries are probably one reason why these also are among the most inconsistent teams in the league. It seems like the Packers have a lot of injuries. But is that true? Here's some good injury data shared by @RotoWire . ⬇️ https://t.co/Mp2IlrCeZW The Packers can’t get out of their own way on offense, which is why they’ve scored 20 or fewer points in four of seven games. They scored only 17 points last week against the Lions, who have one of the worst defenses in the NFL. Detroit entered the game on pace to blow away the dubious league record for passing yards allowed. Jordan Love and Co. failed miserably to capitalize, especially in key moments. The Panthers are no better. Remember Green Bay’s loss to Atlanta at Lambeau? That came just days after Carolina went into Atlanta and won by 31. The Panthers had won three of their last four games until getting steamrolled 43-13 by the Buccaneers. So, which team(s) will show up tonight? So, let’s bring it back to injuries. The Panthers’ starting cornerbacks, Mike Jackson and Jaycee Horn, are on injured reserve. Their best pass rusher, Jaelan Phillips, will be inactive due to injury. So, there should be opportunities for the Packers to make plays in the passing game. Combined with a matchup against the worst run defense in the NFL, this could be a breakout game for Green Bay’s offense. “Should be,” of course, is the operative phrase. The only thing the Packers do consistently is play inconsistently. They can’t run the football. They struggle to protect the passer. They drop passes. They misfire on third down and squander opportunities in the red zone. So, should the Packers have a big game offensively? Yes. But will they? At least the defense is good, with Gannon earning his paycheck by fielding a formidable unit that has mostly played winning football even though it can’t rush the passer with a traditional four-man rush. So, who wins? I’d give the advantages to Green Bay on both sides of the ball. On offense, Love should have a strong game against Carolina’s depleted pass defense. Heck, they might even be able to run the football against the league’s worst rush defense. On defense, the Packers have spoken highly of Panthers quarterback Bryce Young all week, but Young is not as good as Detroit’s Jared Goff and the Panthers have only one big-time threat in the passing game compared to two for Detroit. The Panthers will be without their preferred starting offensive tackles, too. So, the Packers will score a key win. A 5-3 start with Micah Parsons still not back on the practice field would be a major victory for a team that has aspirations to be playing deep into January. Bill’s Prediction: Packers 27, Panthers 17. Bill’s Record: 5-2. Here are the 10 most important Packers for tonight's game, a story filled with quotes and other good stuff by @JacobWestendorf . ⬇️ https://t.co/tX2pc7MrfW Jacob Westendorf’s Packers-Panthers Prediction I don't think this game is going to be pretty. Matt LaFleur said earlier this week that Panthers coordinator Ejiro Evero's defense forces everyone on offense to be consistent on every single play. The Packers have not been like that all season. The injuries on the offensive line make for some uncertainty, and give this coaching staff a chance to screw up the starting five combination, like they have so many times in the past. That being said, Carolina is missing some big guns on defense, including their star pass rusher. Even if Matthew Golden cannot go or is on limited reps, Christian Watson and Tucker Kraft should be able to make enough plays in the passing game. Perhaps Josh Jacobs can finally find some room to roam on the ground against the league's worst run defense. Expect a sloppy game, but the Packers will make one more play than the Panthers, getting them to 5-3 before a much-needed mini bye week. Jacob’s Prediction: Packers 17, Panthers 14. away.headline: Packers list four questionable, rule out three vs. Panthers | Week 8 Injury Report
away.blurb: Packers list four questionable, rule out three vs. Panthers | Week 8 Injury Report Skip to main content Primary nav News WR Matthew Golden, DT Devonte Wyatt questionable for Thursday night Evan Siegle, packers.com WR Matthew Golden Oct. 29 update: CB Keisean Nixon (shoulder) has been added to the injury report and is questionable for tonight's contest against the Carolina Panthers. GREEN BAY – The Packers have listed receiver Matthew Golden (shoulder/foot), defensive tackles Devonte Wyatt (ankle) and Anthony Campbell (ankle), and edge rusher Brenton Cox Jr. (quadricep) as questionable for Thursday night against Carolina. Green Bay has ruled out linebacker Zaire Franklin (shin), guard/tackle Travis Glover (knee) and center Sean Rhyan (ankle). Golden and Wyatt briefly exited during Sunday's 20-17 loss in Detroit but returned to finish the game. Both were estimated as nonparticipants on Monday's injury report before being upgraded to limited (Wyatt on Tuesday and Golden on Wednesday). Head Coach Matt LaFleur said Tuesday evening he was hopeful Golden might be available against the Panthers. The Packers have not stated who will start against Carolina in place of Rhyan and Glover but have several options. Kevin Zeitler , Jager Burton and Donovan Jennings were all healthy scratches in Detroit while veteran Aaron Banks (knee/toe) will be available against Carolina after being promoted to full participation Friday. In addition to Banks, cornerback Benjamin St-Juste (hamstring) didn't receive a game status and will be available against the Panthers. away.blurb: After missing three games due to a dislocated thumb on his throwing hand, quarterback Baker Mayfield is back in the lineup for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday as they take on the Carolina Panthers in a critical intra-division game. Mayfield carried a questionable designation on the injury report into the weekend but was able to practice without limitations throughout the week. He intends to wear a specialized glove on his right hand that offers added support to the injured joint, preventing the thumb from being bent backward. Mayfield will not have the team's top receiving target at his disposal, however, as wide receiver Emeka Egbuka is out for Week Seven with both a concussion and a foot injury. In addition, starting right tackle Luke Goedeke is out due to a calf ailment and safety Antoine Winfield Jr. will miss his third straight outing thanks to a rib fracture. After elevating linebacker Caden Fordham from the practice squad, the Buccaneers had 54 available players and thus had to name six inactives to get down to the game-day limit of 48. The Panthers also elevated outside linebacker Nick Hampton and cornerback Robert Rochell from the practice squad and had to name seven inactive players. Carolina will be without one of its top pass-rushers as Jaelan Phillips is out due to a hamstring strain. Fellow outside linebacker Thomas Incoom is also unavailable due to a calf issue, and he was placed on injured reserve on Saturday. away.blurb: So can the Panthers sustain their recent success? Will Mayfield’s return yield a new hope? Will the NFC South standings be shaken up? Fans can also check the game out on radio: WRFX The Fox, 99.7 FM. Anish Shroff (play-by-play), Luke Kuechly (analyst), Jake Delhomme (analyst), Jim Szoke (host), Kristen Balboni (sideline). For full local listings, check out the Carolina Panthers Radio Network . Special note: Kuechly will receive his Pro Football Hall of Fame ring at halftime of the game in Bank of America Stadium. Out: OLB Thomas Incoom (calf), OLB Jaelan Phillips (hamstring) Questionable: OT Monroe Freeling (knee), LB Bam Martin-Scott (hamstring) Out: WR Emeka Egbuka (concussion/foot), OT Luke Goedeke (calf), S Antoine Winfield (rib) Questionable: QB Baker Mayfield (right thumb) Alex Zietlow: Panthers 35, Bucs 31. I know that Baker Mayfield’s almost-certain return will make this Bucs offense more dynamic. And I know that scoring 35 on this Bucs team will be difficult, considering their opportunistic defensive backfield and their Top 5 rush defense. Still, barring an implosion of turnovers, I think the Panthers outscore and outlast a Bucs team trying to get back on track. Can the Carolina Panthers make it three wins in a row? And can the Tampa Bay Buccaneers get back on track? The Panthers (3-2) are returning to Bank of America Stadium for their Week 7 contest (1 p.m., FOX) fresh off two statement victories against the Detroit Lions and the Philadelphia Eagles . They’re looking to go 4-2 for the first time as a franchise since 2019 and start 2-0 in the NFC South for the first time since 2022. Carolina ranks first in the NFL in passing yards per game (295.6), second in total yards per game (404.4) and fourth in points per game (29.2). And its defense — minus the Week 1 fiasco against the Bears that’s looking more and more like an aberration — is Top 10 in several statistics, including rushing yards allowed. The Panthers have allowed fewer than 50 yards in each of the last two weeks: 46 against the Lions, 35 against the Eagles. It’s true that the defense is a bit affected by injury, specifically at the outside linebacker spot with no Jaelan Phillips or Thomas Incoom this week . It’s also true that the defense has only had to play against starting quarterbacks three times so far this season, and two of those three — against Caleb Williams of the Bears and Deshaun Watson of the Browns — have yielded losses. That won’t happen this week; it looks like the Bucs will be led by Baker Mayfield, who’s missed the last few weeks with a dislocated thumb on his throwing hand. Speaking of the Bucs (1-5): While many of their offensive stats might be skewed by Mayfield’s absence, many of their strengths will remain. Namely? Their rush defense. Tampa Bay ranks second in the NFL in rush yards allowed per game at 75.5, thanks to a defensive line anchored by nose tackle Vita Vea and an entire unit led by rookie linebacker Josiah Trotter. home.blurb: The Green Bay Packers expect superstar pass rusher Micah Parsons to return to practice next week, according to a report from NFL Network insider Ian Rapoport on Thursday. “Micah Parsons is expected to return to practice next week. home.headline: Green Bay Packers: Micah Parsons sounds off on NFL officials following team’s Week 7 loss to Lions
home.blurb: Josh Jacobs says he is remorseful in first comments since Packers return Green Bay Packers: Micah Parsons sounds off on NFL officials following team’s Week 7 loss to Lions - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL WNBA Finals: Dream force Game 7 Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Green Bay Packers fell to the Detroit Lions on Sunday afternoon by the score of 20-17. Unfortunately, issues that have plagued the team all year, such as injuries, dropped passes, and missed kicks, reared their ugly heads again in Week Seven. Indeed, had the Packers played fundamental and mistake-free football, they would have won the game. After all, the Lions needed a field goal in the closing seconds of the contest in order to win. After the game was over, though, a great deal of criticism was directed at the NFL officials who refereed the game, including by one Packers player who was not able to participate: Micah Parsons . Green Bay Packers star Micah Parsons criticizes NFL officials Green Bay Packers defensive end Micah Parsons (1) celebrates his sack during the fourth quarter of their game Sunday, September 7, 2025 at Lambeau Field in Green Bay, Wisconsin. The Green Bay Packers beat the Detroit Lions 27-13. For their part, the Packers players themselves are not making excuses for the loss. That is, they are not at all saying that the reason they lost in Detroit was because of the officials. However, they are frustrated with the confusing calls made against them. Multiple players expressed their frustration about bogus roughing the passer calls while Jordan Love was mugged without any flags being thrown. They just want the game called fairly. Parsons, for his part, posted the following message on social media: This particular post is a reference, specifically, to how Brenton Cox was literally pushed into Lions quarterback Jared Goff and whistled for roughing the passer. Over the last several weeks, Green Bay players have been called for this penalty just for putting their hands on an opposing quarterback. At some point, something is going to have to change regarding how the officials are calling Packers games. Even the national media, including Tom Brady, thought the games was terrible in terms of how one-sided the referees were. The Packers won the game, 27-13. The Minnesota Vikings are the only remaining undefeated team in the NFL, as the San Francisco 49ers were handed their first loss by the Atlanta Falcons , while the Kansas City Chiefs took their first "L" to the Seattle Seahawks . The Vikings have a massive matchup this week, as they take on the high-flying Lions in Detroit. Elsewhere around the NFL , Lamar Jackson looks to make his return to the field against Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills , the Cleveland Browns and Pittsburgh Steelers face off for the second time in the last month, and the Chicago Bears travel out west to play Sam Darnold and the Seahawks. Which teams should you pick in Week 8, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Oct. 27 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. Credit to CBS Sports Research Carolina Panthers at Green Bay Packers (-3.5) (TNF) Dajani ( Packers -3.5): I'm willing to overlook the Carolina Panthers ' surprising 43-13 loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . They are a better team than what they showed last Sunday, but it's difficult to overlook the fact that Carolina's rushing defense ranks dead last in the NFL with 153.2 yards allowed per game. Josh Jacobs rushed for just 36 yards on 11 carries last week against the Lions in his 2026 debut, but I think he's in for a massive homecoming in primetime on a short week. I'm not saying the Packers run away with this one, but I'll take them to cover 3.5 points. … Prediction: Packers 27, Panthers 23 Dubin (Packers -3.5): It was surprising to see the Panthers get smacked in the face by the Buccaneers last week. The Packers probably can't do the same thing the Bucs did — run the ball down Carolina's throat — but they can still beat that defense with explosive plays. With the top two cornerbacks still out, Christian Watson and Matthew Golden (if he plays) are going to be able to find space in the defense. Green Bay's own defense has also played better of late after a rough start to the season. … Prediction: Packers 24, Panthers 17 Baltimore Ravens at Buffalo Bills (-3.5) Dajani ( Ravens +3.5): Ignore that Baltimore allowed 35 unanswered points to the Cincinnati Bengals last week, because it appears that Lamar Jackson is back! He was playing some legitimate MVP-level ball before getting hurt, as Jackson went 3-1 as the starter, while completing 70.8% of his passes with 10.1 yards per attempt, six passing touchdowns and just one interception. Only four quarterbacks have put up those kinds of numbers in their first four starts of a season in the past 40 years. The Ravens are a completely different team with Jackson under center, and this Bills defense allows too many points. Buffalo ranks third-worst in scoring defense (28.5 ppg), and has allowed at least 30 points in four of its five victories this season. Jackson is 10-5 SU and 13-2 ATS as an underdog in his career. He's statistically the best quarterback to bet on when listed as an underdog since 1970. … Prediction: Ravens 30, Bills 28 Dubin (Ravens +3.5): This is the same deal as with the Ravens and me pretty much every week: flip the pick if Lamar Jackson sits out again. Otherwise, I like the Ravens to at least keep things close against the Bills. Both of these offenses have been pretty excellent, and the Ravens have been especially so when Jackson has been on the field with Zay Flowers . Ultimately, though, the Bills' home-field advantage and the weaknesses in Baltimore's own pass defense lead me to take the Bills to win and the Ravens to cover. … Prediction: Bills 30, Ravens 27 Minnesota Vikings at Detroit Lions (-3) Dajani (Lions -3): I'm shocked by this line, honestly. The only remaining undefeated team in the NFL is a three-point underdog to a division rival? With that said, I think I agree with it. The Vikings' defense is the main reason they are 5-0, as they've allowed a league-leading 12.3 points per game, plus registered a league-leading 10.6% sack rate and 47.6% pressure rate. Offensively, the Vikings have the fewest touchdowns (10) by a 6-0 team since the 1934 Lions and rank 31st in offensive EPA. They could have lost last week to the Indianapolis Colts , who are in the midst of a fire sale. As for the Lions, the concern has always been with their defense. But I think Kelvin Sheppard 's unit is coming along. They allowed just 17 points to the Packers last week, and Brian Branch is back in the lineup. Maybe we could see a push here, but I'm taking the Lions to win … Prediction: Lions 24, Vikings 20 Dubin (Lions -3): Detroit has recently been thrown off its offensive game by Brian Flores' defense, but the offense is operating at an extremely high level right now, with Jared Goff playing as well as he has in recent memory. And as Dajani said, this Minnesota offense just does not have the ability to get into a high-scoring game and come away with a win. They need the defense to hold the opponent down entirely, and I'm not sure that even Flores' bunch can do that in the friendly confines of Ford Field. … Prediction: Lions 23, Vikings 14 Cleveland Browns at Pittsburgh Steelers (-3.5) Dajani (Steelers -3.5): How can the Browns keep getting away with this? They overcame a 14-0 deficit in Nashville on Sunday, as Harold Fannin Jr . took a short reception 36 yards down the field with 20 seconds remaining to set up a 32-yard game-winning field goal from Andre Szmyt . Deshaun Watson became the third quarterback since 1970 to register a game-winning drive in each of his team's first five wins of the season. With this being a divisional game against an opponent that just got back from Paris, I can understand why some would take the points with the underdog given the hook. But the Steelers are 3-0 ATS at home. That includes Week 3, when they dropped 30 points on Joe Burrow and the Bengals in a win, and Week 5, when Pittsburgh scored 34 points in a double-digit victory over the Colts. The Steelers are averaging 26.0 points per game over their last five contests, which ranks top 10 in the NFL, and are 8-0 SU and ATS in their last eight home games vs. the Browns. In fact, Pittsburgh is actually a perfect 11-0 ATS in its last 11 home divisional games. Insane stat. … Prediction: Steelers 26, Browns 21 Dubin (Steelers -3.5): I don't understand how the Browns keep doing it. Every single one of their victories has required a game-winning drive in the final five minutes of the game. That's not sustainable on any level whatsoever. The Steelers don't exactly have consistency written all over them, considering the vagaries of their passing game and the fact that their three-game winning streak has come against weak opponents. However, I trust Jaylen Warren and Co. more than I do the Browns at this point. … Prediction: Steelers 20, Browns 13 Atlanta Falcons at Tampa Bay Buccaneers (-2.5) Dajani (Falcons +2.5): I have plenty of questions about both of these teams, but I did tell you the Falcons were going to cover the small number vs. the 49ers last week! Atlanta finished that game on a 26-6 run after trailing 14-3. They scored on four straight drives. I'm not sure the Buccaneers deserve to be three-point favorites this week after that destruction of the Panthers. Baker Mayfield had to throw for just 64 yards and a touchdown in a 43-13 victory, as Bucky Irving , Kenneth Gainwell and Sean Tucker combined for 246 yards rushing and three touchdowns. This Falcons rush defense ranks fourth in the NFL with 88.9 rushing yards allowed per game. Plus, the Falcons have won two road games this season by 20+ points after being listed as an underdog, and are 4-0 ATS in their last four road games against the Buccaneers. … Prediction: Falcons 26, Buccaneers 24 Dubin (Falcons +2.5): The Buccaneers ran all over the Panthers last week, but Atlanta has actually been quite good against the run, allowing only 3.8 yards per carry this season. Can Tampa really control the game with Bucky Irving the way it did last week, or will it have to actually turn Baker Mayfield loose as a passer here? If the Bucs have to do that, I have more confidence in Atlanta's offense right now, with Bijan Robinson , Drake London and even Kyle Pitts contributing at a high level. … Prediction: Falcons 23, Buccaneers 17 Kansas City Chiefs (-1.5) at Denver Broncos Dajani ( Broncos +1.5): The Broncos had an embarrassing outing last time they played the Chiefs, allowing 247 yards off of 28 missed tackles in a 31-10 loss. There has been a lot of talk about Bo Nix and the offense, but what about the Chiefs? They averaged 4.3 yards per play and recorded just 213 yards of total offense in that embarrassing loss to the Seahawks. The team seemingly never got off the bus. The Baltimore Ravens are trending toward getting Lamar Jackson back for Sunday's Week 8 matchup against the Buffalo Bills. Jackson has missed each of the team's last three games after suffering a high-ankle sprain in Week 4. The Ravens are 1-2 over that stretch, losing each of their last two matchups against the division-rival Cleveland Browns and Cincinnati Bengals. On Wednesday, Jackson started the week of practice with full participation. Given his full participation early in the week, it appears Jackson will be good to go this coming Sunday — barring any injury setbacks. The Ravens began their 2026 campaign with a 4-1 start, but have since dropped to 4-3. RB Adam Randall (neck, designated to return from IR) CB T.J. Tampa (knee, designated to return from IR) * The rest of the squad is in relatively good shape heading into Sunday. home.blurb: According to The Athletic's Jeff Zrebiec, Ioane was on the practice field Thursday after missing Wednesday's session with the knee injury. His return is particularly encouraging considering initial reports suggested the Ravens' first-round pick would miss time, potentially forcing Baltimore into another offensive line adjustment ahead of Sunday's matchup against the Buffalo Bills . Ioane suffered the injury during the first half against Cincinnati after taking contact to his knee while attempting to block downfield. He exited the game and did not return, with Emery Jones Jr. replacing him at right guard. Ioane's return to practice suggests he could be progressing faster than anticipated, although his participation level and availability for Sunday's game remain uncertain. Head coach Jesse Minter declined to rule out Ioane earlier this week, acknowledging the rookie's toughness while emphasizing that Baltimore would evaluate his recovery before making a decision. The Ravens acquired veteran center Cam Jurgens from Philadelphia earlier this month, allowing Ioane to return to guard while providing Baltimore with a more experienced presence in the middle of the offensive line. The Ravens were preparing for the possibility of starting Jones or Andrew Vorhees at right guard against Buffalo, but Ioane's return could provide another option if he continues progressing. The potential return of Lamar Jackson from a high ankle sprain makes offensive line stability even more important as the Ravens attempt to protect their quarterback and establish a more balanced attack. Baltimore will continue monitoring Ioane's knee ahead of Friday's final injury report. His return to the field is encouraging, but the Ravens must still determine whether he can handle the demands of Sunday's matchup against Buffalo. Especially after last week’s blown two-score lead to the Cleveland Browns, nobody is expecting Robert Saleh’s first team in Nashville to execute a miraculous turnaround. Draft discussions are already becoming relevant, if that tells you anything. Still, the Titans hit the road to face the Cincinnati Bengals this coming Sunday, and it’s a chance for Tennessee to win their second game in three weeks. That’s somehow still an exciting prospect. To preview the matchup, I’ve got one reason the Titans will beat the Bengals, one reason they won’t, and my own prediction for what will actually happen. Let’s start with the former. Will: Titans’ secondary sees massive uptick Two weeks in a row now, Tennessee has forced at least one interception. The Titans have come down with three picks over the last two games, two of which belong to rising offseason pickup Cor’Dale Flott. Tennessee Titans cornerback Cor'dale Flott (18) intercepts Indianapolis Colts quarterback Daniel Jones (17) on Sunday, Oct. 18, 2026, at Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect The Bengals score a lot - a lot - of points. TeamRankings has Cincinnati fourth in the NFL in points per game (27.2) and touchdowns per game (3.2). Their passing statistics specifically are top 10 across the board regarding pass play percentage, completion percentage, and pass yards per game. The Bengals score a lot - a lot - of points. TeamRankings has Cincinnati fourth in the NFL in points per game (27.2) and touchdowns per game (3.2). Their passing statistics specifically are top 10 across the board regarding pass play percentage, completion percentage, and pass yards per game. Tennessee is facing one of the best pass-first teams in the NFL. If Saleh's secondary can find consistency beyond the occasional turnover, the Titans would have more than a fair chance to shut down RB Chase Brown on the ground, too. It's much easier to stop Joe Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase, and Tee Higgins in concept than it is on the field, but doing so is the Titans' key to winning this one. Won’t: Titans can't overcome inconsistent Bengals defense The inverse, of course, is if the Titans' offense continues to suffer. The Bengals have proved themselves beatable against "bad" teams - just see their narrow, one-score win over the 1-6 Miami Dolphins two weeks ago. But Cincinnati also just dismantled the Baltimore Ravens last week, 35-13. The through line is that Cincy scored 30+ points in both of those contests; it comes down to the opposing offense's ability to hang in there when Burrow and his crew get hot. Tennessee ranks 31st in both touchdowns and points per game. Almost everywhere the Bengals are in the top 10 through the air, the Titans are in the bottom 10. Cincy has allowed 20+ points in four of their six games this season. If Cam Ward can get back on his feet in any sense of the saying, another 24-point performance like Tennessee had last week could be enough to at least make this one interesting. However, the Titans may need a little more juice than they've seen yet this season from their QB to stay in it. Prediction: Titans lose, 31-20 Ultimately, I have the Titans falling to 1-7 in this one. We've seen a number of trends solidify that this roster has failed to prove their ability to rise beyond. Carnell Tate is the primary receiver in an otherwise underwhelming offense. The defense can force early turnovers, but can't get late stops when it matters - especially when it comes to tackling. Ward has a better second half than his typically abysmal first, but by the time Tennessee tries to get aggressive, it's too late to make a difference. I expect most of, if not all of these notes to be hit in Week 8. I don't think the Titans will lose in a blowout, but on the road against one of the best offenses in the league, this one already looks like too much for Saleh's team. picks.headline: Titans scouting report vs Cincinnati Bengals, matchups, prediction NFL Week 8
picks.blurb: News Sports Counties Business Real Estate Advertise Obituaries eNewspaper Legals TITANS Titans scouting report vs Cincinnati Bengals, matchups, prediction NFL Week 8 Tyler Palmateer Nashville Tennessean Oct. 28, 2026, 5:04 a.m. CT The Tennessee Titans will face the Cincinnati Bengals in NFL Week 8 following a 27-24 loss to the Cleveland Browns. The Bengals' passing offense, led by quarterback Joe Burrow, poses a significant challenge to the Titans' struggling defense. Positives are hard to find amid the Tennessee Titans’ struggles, but running back Tony Pollard was one last week. The Memphis native had his second-best game as a Titans player, with 129 yards rushing and three touchdowns on 25 carries in a gutting 27-24 home loss to the Cleveland Browns on Oct. 25. Maybe Pollard can do it again when the Titans (1-6) face the Cincinnati Bengals (4-2) at Paycor Stadium on Nov. 1 (noon CT, CBS) in NFL Week 8. The Bengals' and Browns ' run defenses are about the same statistically. Cincinnati allows 116.3 rushing yards per game, which ranks 19th in the league. The Titans gained a season-high 322 yards of offense with Pollard’s contributions, taking pressure off developing second-year quarterback Cam Ward . Tennessee coach Robert Saleh pinned the Browns loss on defense . Now that unit will face Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow, who’s 11th in the league with 1,653 yards passing, and second with 15 passing touchdowns, to go with three interceptions. Here’s our scouting report for the Titans’ game against the Browns. One Cincinnati Bengals stat to know Cincinnati has 13 pass plays of 25 yards or more this season. Tennessee has seven. Where Tennessee Titans have edge vs. Bengals The good news: Cincinnati’s offense ranks 29th in rushing yards per game (81.2), so there’s an opportunity for the Titans to make the Bengals one-dimensional. The bad news: Cincinnati’s offense is doing fine without a rushing threat, averaging 345.2 yards. It isn’t a big Titans advantage, but they must capitalize on it and see if stopping the run allows their pass rush to play like it did against the Colts (six sacks). It will take a stark turnaround after Tennessee allowed a season-high 183 yards rushing against the Browns. That marked the franchise’s worst single-game Pro Football Focus run defense grade (36.3) since 2023. Personnel changes up front have not helped. Run-stopping defensive tackle Jordan Elliott was released on Oct. 20 after breaking the NFL's gun policy . Third-year defender Timmy Horne was signed from the practice squad to replace him. Where Cincinnati Bengals have edge vs. Titans Tennessee’s secondary tackled poorly and took bad angles against the Browns, making rookie receiver KC Concepcion look like a Pro Bowler (eight catches, 129 yards). Imagine what Burrow and receivers Tee Higgins and Ja’Marr Chase might do. The Titans haven't seen an offense like this in 2026. The Bengals are seventh in the league in passing yards per game (264) and get 76% of their total yards through the air. Higgins and Chase have accounted for nine of the Bengals’ 13 explosive pass plays. Saleh’s also soul-searching in his secondary. Alontae Taylor was signed in the offseason to fortify one of Tennessee’s outside corner spots, but he was made inactive in Week 6 by coach’s decision and didn’t see the field in Week 7. Now it looks like Taylor will likely move to nickel . This would be a good week for Taylor to make a contribution, assuming Saleh plays him. Score prediction: Bengals 35, Titans 21 The Titans' scarred defense won’t be able to slow Burrow, and they can’t depend on Ward to keep pace in a shootout. It looks like their worst-case scenario matchup. Winning the turnover battle and making a few plays on special teams would help, but the Titans will be fortunate to keep it within 14 points. Tyler Palmateer covers the Tennessee Titans for The Tennessean. Have a story idea for Tyler? Reach him at tpalmateer@tennessean.com and on the X platform, @tpalmateer83 .

away.blurb: Chase was in concussion protocol and listed as questionable for the Miami game. After a 4-yard catch from Burrow against Jacksonville, Chase had his facemask grabbed by Jags defensive back Jarrian Jones . Chase went to the ground and took a big hit from linebacker Ventrell Miller. Asked how he was feeling when he talked to reporters later in the day, Chase said , "Good." "(The ankle's) doing well," Chase added. "I practiced today the whole time." Chase, who didn't practice Oct. 28, also said he played through the injury during his five-catch, 62-yard, one-touchdown effort in the team's Week 7 rout of Baltimore. over the Eagles. Dallas sits second in the NFC East, one and a half games behind the Giants. Arizona sits in the cellar in the NFC West already four games behind the 49ers. Dallas’ win 38-21 Monday night was its most encouraging performance of the season. Dak Prescott threw for 212 yards and three touchdowns without an interception, including two scores to CeeDee Lamb , as the Cowboys erased a 21-20 third-quarter deficit and scored the final 18 points. We buried the headline, however. Javonte Williams rushed for a career-high 155 yards and a touchdown, helping Dallas pile up 204 rushing yards. Arizona’s latest loss illustrated one of its biggest problems. The Cardinals produced 353 yards and controlled the ball for more than 33 minutes against Denver, but went just 1-for-5 in the red zone in the 30-16 defeat. Quarterback Jacoby Brissett completed 27 of 48 passes for 272 yards and a touchdown, with Trey McBride catching 10 passes for 111 yards and the score. Offensively, Dallas has been considerably more productive, averaging 27.0 points and 353.6 yards per game, compared with Arizona’s 20.3 points and 313.9 yards. The Cardinals do own the better turnover differential at plus-2, compared with minus-3 for Dallas, giving Arizona one potential route to an upset Sunday. Dallas’ biggest storyline Sunday is whether the Prescott-Lamb passing game and Williams-led rushing attack can sustain the balance they finally showed against Philadelphia. The Cardinals have been one of the best teams at winning the time of possession battle but one of the worst in the red zone. They must find a way to turn their long drives into touchdowns. Recent history is important here, particularly because Arizona has repeatedly caused Dallas problems of late. The Cowboys lead the all-time series 56-36-1, but Arizona has won four straight regular-season meetings. Arizona won 27-17 in their most recent meeting against Dallas on November 3, 2025. That last meeting has particular relevance because Brissett and Prescott were also the quarterbacks: Brissett, starting with Kyler Murray sidelined, went 21-of-31 for 261 yards and two touchdowns and also ran for a score, while Prescott threw for 250 yards with one touchdown and an interception and was sacked five times. Arizona committed no turnovers, Dallas committed three, and the Cardinals converted three of four red-zone possessions into touchdowns. The Arizona Cardinals gave him the most guaranteed money of any running back in NFL history when they selected him with the third-overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft , and it's easy to see why. The Notre Dame product dominated at the collegiate level, routinely flashing his elite athleticism and ability to make plays both as a runner and a returner. In theory, he has the talent to be a true three-down workhorse like Atlanta's Bijan Robinson and Detroit's Jahmyr Gibbs . Unfortunately for everyone involved, Jeremiyah Love suffered an ankle injury during his first real taste of NFL action. The running back suffered an ankle injury midway through the contest and missed most of the preseason. While he has played in five games despite the injury, NFL Network's Ian Rapoport revealed the running back will not play in Week 7, as the team is resting him in hopes of ensuring his long-term health. | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - David Latham, Managing Editor While Jeremiyah Love has played in every game this season, he hasn't lived up to his pre-draft hype. So far, the running back has recorded just 245 yards and one touchdown on 67 attempts, good for just 3.7 yards per carry. While the Cardinals passing attack and subpar offensive line certainly haven't done anything to ease the pressure on the rookie, he hasn't looked like his college self either. Hopefully, taking some time to rest will help him recapture his previous form. In his absence, free agent signee Tyler Allgeier will likely get the start. The former Atlanta Falcon has had similar struggles behind Arizona's offensive line, recording just 119 yards and one touchdown on 35 attempts throughout the young season. Nolen suffered a calf injury before training camp of his rookie season, which saw him miss the beginning of 2025 before returning halfway through the year. He played a handful of games and showed massive promise before suffering a knee injury that landed him on injured reserve, ending his year. Nolen had surgery (later revealed to be a meniscus) but made a full recovery and was healthy for 2026's training camp, though he suffered a minor lower body injury during the team's time at State Farm Stadium. Their defensive line pressure rate of 24.7% ranks dead-last in the league. In a front seven that's been largely uninspiring, Nolen's presence has been noticeable on a weekly basis. picks.blurb: Odds Detroit Lions Beat Minnesota Vikings in Week 8 Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code Fanatics Sportsbook Promo Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Rainbet Promo Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code Novig Promo Code Underdog Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI The Detroit Lions will face a second straight NFC North divisional opponent when they take on the Minnesota Vikings Sunday afternoon. The Vikings, which have yet to lose a game this season (6-0), feature both a bottom-10 offense (20.8 points/game) and the league's top defensive unit. Coordinated by Brian Flores, Minnesota's defense has permitted just 12.3 points a game, and hasn't allowed more than 16 points in a game since Week 2. And most recently, the Vikings surrendered just 10 points in a 16-10 victory over the Indianapolis Colts in Week 7. Additionally, Minnesota has been extremely stout against the pass thus far this season. In fact, Kevin O'Connell's squad has allowed the second-fewest passing yards (930) and the least amount of touchdowns through the air (three) through the season's first seven weeks. The Vikings have also already secured seven interceptions, spearheaded by cornerback Byron Murphy's league-high three picks. So, Lions signal-caller Jared Goff, who has yet to throw an interception in 2026, will face arguably his biggest test of the campaign against Minnesota's stingy pass defense . Then on the opposite side of the ball, Detroit's secondary will receive one of its toughest assignments of the year, going head-to-head with All-Pro wideout Justin Jefferson. Jefferson, who has surpassed 1,000 receiving yards in each of his first six NFL seasons, has accumulated 302 reception yards and three touchdowns in five games this season. He's unquestionably Vikings passer Kyler Murray's go-to target and one of the very best receivers in the game today. Subsequently, D.J. Reed, the Lions’ No. 1 cornerback , should get the majority of one-on-one reps with the Pro Bowl pass-catcher. Additionally, I wouldn't be surprised if Detroit defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard deployed a rotation of corners in the Week 8 tilt. And as a result, I could see the likes of Ennis Rakestraw and Roger McCreary also getting opportunities to defend Jefferson Sunday. It'll hardly be an easy task for the Lions’ defensive backs group. However, Detroit does have a solid track record against Jefferson, having limited him to under 60 yards the past three meetings between the NFC North rivals . And if the Lions could do it a fourth straight time, it would go a long way toward Dan Campbell's squad notching its fifth victory on the season. At this present juncture, I'm willing to give Detroit a 61 percent chance to secure the Week 8 victory . picks.headline: Vikings vs. Lions Final Score Predictions: Experts weigh in on the elite matchup between Jared Goff and Brian Flores

Dec 25, 2025; Minneapolis, Minnesota, USA; Minnesota Vikings linebacker Dallas Turner (15) celebrates after a play as Detroit Lions quarterback Jared Goff (16) reacts in the second half at U.S. Bank Stadium. Matt Krohn-Imagn Images Kole Noble, Mike Payton, Tyler Forness, Wendell Ferreira Thu, October 29, 2026 at 11:00 AM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Minnesota Vikings are undefeated with an elite defense, but this is their first big test with the Detroit Lions. In Week 7, the Minnesota Vikings will be facing their third NFC North opponent of the season, and second on the road when they face the Detroit Lions on Sunday afternoon. The game is a battle between two of the best units in the NFL, with Brian Flores' defense trending at a historic pace against a Lions offense that has consistently made things difficult on the Vikings. Jared Goff has been the key to that success, finding ways to attack Flores' blitz heavy scheme. Even with that success, it didn't resonate last season, as the Vikings won both games. Will that trend continue? Our experts predicted the pivotal NFC North game. Vikings 16, Lions 10 We can talk about how this matchup is one of the bigger ones across the league, especially this week with both teams with a winning record, but the one matchup that has me curious is Flores vs. Goff. We've seen a really interesting split with how much success Goff has had at quarterback against Flores. Goff with Ben Johnson: 4-0 Goff without Johnson: 0-2 Johnson without Goff: 1-2 Are we sure that the combination of Goff and Johnson was the secret sauce together and not just one of them? With how Flores has evolved the defense, the short routes over the middle of the field aren't there the way they used to, and that will be the difference. – Tyler Forness , A to Z Minnesota (2-2 record) Vikings 20, Bears 14 The Minnesota Vikings have been winning games with a clear formula the last few weeks and that formula has been dominating teams on defense. Until a team actually finds a way to get the better of Brian Flores' unit, I'm going to side with Minnesota. Detroit certainly has a lot of firepower on offense to score a ton of points, but Flores held this offense to 10 and 24 points in their last two matchups. In those last two games, quarterback Jared Goff was sacked 5 times in each game. We all know that if you get pressure on Goff up the middle, he's going to struggle. Minnesota has been pressuring the quarterback better than anyone this season. I see the Vikings scoring just enough points to secure a seventh straight win while Flores puts Goff in a blender yet again. – Kole Noble , A to Z Chicago (0-4 record) Lions 23, Vikings 17 This is a wild matchup because, by EPA/play, the Lions are third on offense and 32nd on defense, while the Vikings are first on defense and 30th on offense. So it's a two-headed matchup with strength versus strength and weakness versus weakness. However, my inclination is to think the Lions have a slight advantage despite the challenges of facing a Brian Flores' defense. Since Flores took over as the Vikings defensive coordinator in 2023, the Lions have averaged 26 points a game versus Minnesota. Outside of the second game last year, when the Lions scored 10, it's been consistently good. Jared Goff has been protected, the communication along the offensive line has been excellent, and that's how you make Goff play at his highest level. The Lions' secondary is bad, but it certainly got better with Brian Branch getting back. And up front, it's been mostly a viable performance. So, I'm going with Detroit in this one. – Wendell Ferreira , A to Z Green Bay (1-3 record) Lions 17, Vikigns 14 Ultimately, it's going to come down to who can score in this game, and while the Vikings' defense is on the verge of being historically good, the Lions' offense is arguably the best in the league right now, and they get this game at home. It's not going to be easy. It should be a back-and-forth affair all day long, and it should be an ugly one. But I have the Lions winning 17-14 and ending the Vikings' undefeated streak. – Mike Payton , A to Z Detroit (2-2 record) Final Prediction for Vikings vs. Bears Last week, our NFC North beat writers were split on the Vikings against the Green Bay Packers, and this week is no different. It's a fascinating matchup, and the curious element will be the Bears' offense. Are they who we think they are, or a flash in the pan like the 2024 New Orleans Saints with Klint Kubiak? Despite the Vikings being the last undefeated team standing, the folks over at FanDuel Sportsbook believe the 1972 Dolphins will be sipping champagne next Sunday and have set the opening betting line at Lions -3 points . The Vikings' biggest offseason moves included signing starting quarterback Kyler Murray and WR3 Jauan Jennings, as well as trading away EDGE Jonathan Greenard to the Eagles. While the offense gained and the defense lost talent, the results on the field in 2026 couldn't be more opposite. The Vikings defense has been dominant and the primary reason Minnesota is undefeated. They are the top defense in DVOA, but not just overall; they also rank No. 1 in defending the pass and No. 3 in defending the run. They allow teams to score only 12.3 points, on average, and are holding teams to 253 yards of total offense. They're playing at an incredibly high level. On offense, we see the other end of the spectrum. The Vikings offense ranks 27th in DVOA, 27th in the passing game, and 22nd in rushing. They average 20.8 points per game, but much of that is because their defense sets them up in many favorable situations. The Lions are still working out some of the kinks in their roster, but there have been noticeable signs of improvement, and it doesn't take much for the offense to catch fire quickly. This will be a true good-vs.-good matchup on Sunday afternoon at Ford Field, as the Lions' explosive offense will do their best to find cracks in a defense that doesn't have many flaws. Vikings vs. Lions bold predictions for NFC North clash in Week 8 Douglas Fritz, ClutchPoints Tue, October 27, 2026 at 2:38 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads As the Minnesota Vikings plan their next massive blitz, the Detroit Lions ride the wave of a big division win. These teams meet in Week 8, and here are bold predictions for the NFC North clash. It's a critical game for the Lions. The NFC North could end up with only two playoff teams. That's because the 49ers, Seahawks, and Rams still seem like firm bets. And that leaves only one other Wild Card spot. The Lions stand at 4-2 while the Vikings are 6-0. A loss would leave the Lions three games back of first place with nearly half the season in the rearview mirror. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Lions RB Jahmyr Gibbs will rush for 100-plus yards It's tough to throw against the Vikings. They rank No. 2 in the NFL against the pass, allowing just 155 yards per game. And while their run defense is good, it's still the better path to consistently moving the football. Gibbs is fourth in the NFL with 620 yards through six games. Look for the Lions to put a saddle on him against the Vikings. Yes, the Lions are clearly overusing Gibbs already. He's almost on a record pace , according to NBC Sports. "If Gibbs keeps to his current pace of 27.7 touches per game for the entire 17-game season, he'll finish this season with a whopping 470 touches," Michael David Smith wrote. "That would be the second-most in a season in NFL history, second only to former James Wilder, who had 492 touches with the 1984 Buccaneers." Gibbs should get close to that number of touches on the ground alone. He had 29 carries against the Saints and Packers this season. Look for the neighborhood of 25 against the Vikings. He's averaging 4.6 per carry, so that easily puts him over 100. And don't worry about the injury scare late against the Packers, according to mlive.com. During his postgame media session, Lions coach Dan Campbell confirmed that Gibbs is OK and avoided serious injury . "Yeah, we got him checked," Lions head coach Dan Campbell said. "He should be good. That's that whole, 'Is it really worth going down and try to finish the game, or you just go score?' Sometimes I question that. I don't know, maybe we shouldn't just, but all good. It's a good win." Lions will double the Vikings' season average in points allowed For the season, the Vikings are allowing just 12.3 points per game. Over the last three games, they are giving up just 33 points. But the Lions will hit them for 24-plus points. Not only will Gibbs cut loose, but his runs will set up play-action daggers for Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jameson Williams. This is no timid prediction. The Vikings defense is the real deal. The players will even tell you that , according to The Athletic. "It's a generational group," cornerback Isaiah Rodgers said. "We've got guys who go out and trust the scheme. They trust (Flores and his staff). The stats speak for themselves." Defensive tackle Levi Drake Rodriguez said it is togetherness that brings the good outcomes. "Hopefully, that showed the joy we have on the field with each other," Rodriguez said. "We want to work hard for each other. We want to be right." But the Lions are a different beast. They are king of the offensive jungle for a reason. They rank No. 2 in the NFL with 397.3 yards per game. The NFL used to be a league where great defense would pretty much always shut down a great offense. But the rules have changed. And the Lions will cut loose for a point total the Vikings haven't allowed since 22 in the season opener against the Packers. Vikings QB Kyler Murray will have his best game of the season For all the Lions are on offense, they ain't that on defense. They rank dead last in the league with 391 yards allowed per game. Murray hasn't thrown for 250 yards in a game yet this season. In fact, he hasn't done it since 2024. And he only has three touchdown passes in basically four games played. He missed almost all of the season opener after a first-quarter injury. But the Lions are relatively decent against the run. They are an open gate against the pass. And Murray will take advantage with some chunk plays down the field. Vikings head coach Kevin O'Connell is standing behind Murray, according to The Athletic. "I think our guys are very confident that we're not far off," O'Connell said. "The far-off changes a little bit as you go, but I'm very, very confident we'll get it going." One reason for optimism is that Murray has gotten better at play action. The Vikings used play action on nearly half of Murray's dropbacks in Week 7. And Murray hit on eight of 11 passes. There's still hope for Murray. Some people have been writing him off and saying the Vikings should move on, but this is a chance for him to silence critics. Our friends at the FanDuel Sportsbook have opened the betting lines for Week 8 in the National Football League, and the Vikings are currently a 3-point underdog as they head into their NFC North matchup with the Detroit Lions at Ford Field. The over/under for this one currently rests at 46.5 points. On Sunday, the Vikings once again struggled on offense against a team that they probably shouldn't have struggled against on offense, as they managed to get into the end zone just one time against the Indianapolis Colts. Thanks to another stellar performance by the defense, however, that was enough, as they managed to hold on for a 16-10 victory to push their record to 6-0. With the San Francisco 49ers losing to the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday afternoon and the Kansas City Chiefs falling to the Seattle Seahawks on Sunday Night Football, the Vikings are now the only team in the league that still has a donut in the loss column. Not even the most ardent of Vikings fans would have seen that coming back in August, but that's where we sit heading into the first Sunday in November. Week 7 in Detroit saw a game of "You take it. . .no, you take it" between the Lions and another NFC North rival of ours, the Green Bay Packers. The game featured bad interceptions on both sides and the standard dumb Dan Campbell fourth-down decision, going for it on 4th-and-1 from his own 24-yard line in a 17-17 game with five minutes remaining. That failed fourth down was immediately followed by Green Bay kicker Trey Smack having a 35-yard field goal attempt blocked to preserve the tie. The Lions then pushed the ball down the field far enough for Jake Bates to kick the game-winning field goal and help the Lions escape with a 20-17 win. The Vikings will be looking for their third straight win over the Lions. . .and, apparently, their third straight win as an underdog. . .after sweeping the season series last year. They defeated the Lions in Detroit last year behind three J.J. McCarthy touchdowns in a 27-24 nail-biter, and effectively ended the Lions' season at U.S. Bank Stadium on Christmas Day, forcing six Detroit turnovers in a 23-10 triumph. Do you think that the Vikings should be underdogs heading into this one, folks? Let us know what you think!

picks.headline: 3 Bold Vikings Predictions Heading Into NFC North Collision vs. Lions in Week 8
picks.blurb: 3 Bold Vikings Predictions Heading Into NFC North Collision vs. Lions in Week 8 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Packers defeat Panthers WNBA Finals: Dream force Game 7 Bears land DT Jeffery Simmons Brewers win World Series Celebrate, Milwaukee! 3 Bold Vikings Predictions Heading Into NFC North Collision vs. Lions in Week 8 This week's bold Vikings predictions are here, including one about what WR Justin Jefferson could do against the Lions' defense on Sunday. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Jason Harmon Thu, October 29, 2026 at 7:17 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Just like that, the November gauntlet is here. Your 6-0 Vikings head to Detroit this weekend to battle the 4-2 Lions for the first time since their Christmas matchup last season. With an undefeated record and divisional seeding on the line, the stakes are certainly high. Will this be the week that finally proves the Vikings are worthy of their record ? Will Kyler Murray and the offense finally get on track? Will the defense finally meet their match? Let's dive into my predictions for Sunday's massive matchup. 1. Justin Jefferson hits for 100 receiving yards This may come as a shock, but Justin Jefferson has had only one 100-yard receiving game since Oct. 5, 2025 . With the Vikings' passing game desperate for a spark against a weak Lions pass defense, Sunday may be the perfect chance to stack some yardage. Detroit's defensive back group is shaky, to say the least. The Lions currently allow the most passing yards per game in the NFL, averaging a whopping 291.8. The return of safety Brian Branch last week against the Packers certainly helps their case, especially if fellow safety Kerby Joseph is close behind after being cleared to return to practice. But their cornerback group should give Jefferson plenty of opportunities to gain yardage this weekend. Ennis Rakestraw Jr. was listed as limited in practice on Wednesday , placing even more pressure on D.J. Reed. 2. NFC North rivals combine for seven or more sacks Even though the Lions give up a ton of yardage on defense, their pass rush is not to be ignored. They're tied with the Vikings, Bengals, Broncos, and Texans for a league-leading 21 sacks. Basically, Sunday could be a bad day to be a quarterback at Ford Field. Star pass rusher Aidan Hutchinson and former Viking D.J. Wonnum each have five sacks for the Lions so far, while rising Vikings star Dallas Turner is tied for the third-most sacks in the league with six. I predict both defensive fronts will continue to cause chaos on Sunday, and that there will be at least seven total sacks between both teams. With the Vikings' inconsistent interior offensive line , Kyler Murray will need to be ready to take off to keep that number from getting even higher. 3. The Vikings lose the battle but win the war There is a case to be made that a loss on Sunday would be the best thing for the Vikings with less than two weeks left before the trade deadline . Obviously, you'd love to win every game, but the lessons learned from a loss may actually set this squad up for better long-term success. A loss could actually be quite the learning experience for HC Kevin O'Connell and the Vikings on Sunday. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Vikings' defense has been stellar, but the Lions' high-flying offense presents the hardest challenge they've faced this year. Can the offense be trusted in its current state to step up and score points? If not, the Vikings will likely suffer their first loss of the year and hopefully walk away with valuable lessons from the experience. If it motivates general manager Nolan Teasley to make a splash deal at the deadline , it may prove to be a good outcome in the long run.
