away.headline: Lions’ Jahmyr Gibbs opens up on injury report confusion ahead of Vikings clash
away.blurb: The status of Detroit Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs for their Week 8 meeting with the Minnesota Vikings got a concerning update on Wednesday, when he was listed with a DNP (Did Not Participate) label . Apparently, even Gibbs was surprised that he got an injury designation. “I was confused,” the former Alabama Crimson Tide star running back said, via Brad Galli of The Brad Galli Show. “I just got dinged up a little bit, like a little shoulder thing but I’m good.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Gibbs explained that he got hurt during a play on third down in Week 7’s meeting with the Green Bay Packers at Ford Field in Detroit on Sunday, but said he didn’t suffer anything serious. In any case, Gibbs was a full participant in Thursday’s practice , allaying any fears about him potentially missing the game against the Vikings at home this coming Sunday. The 24-year-old Gibbs has been on a roll this season, especially of late. After torching the Arizona Cardinals for 151 rushing yards and two touchdowns on 25 carries in Week 5’s 45-21 Detroit win, he burned rubber for 116 rushing yards on 29 carries in the Lions’ 20-17 victory over Green Bay . The Vikings have a top-10 defense against the run, as they are allowing 97.8 rushing yards per outing , but Gibbs can still be expected to deliver the goods for Detroit’s offense given his current form. Gibbs is on pace to record his third straight 1,000-yard season with 620 rushing yards to go along with seven touchdowns to date in the 2026 campaign. Like ClutchPoints’ content? away.blurb: Though safety Kerby Joseph made his long-awaited practice return on Wednesday, a number of other Lions stars didn't practice for a variety of reasons. Lions head coach Dan Campbell had said earlier in the day that Detroit was planning to hold some players out. "St.'s doing good, Ennis (Rakestraw Jr.) is doing good. Going to hold them out of practice. We're going to do a walkthrough, and then roll right into practice for a little bit here. So, just kinda, it goes all-in-one. I think those guys will be at walkthrough, but I don't see them out there during the practice portion. I'm going to hold a couple of other guys back just to get them off their feet, but they'll be at walkthrough," Campbell said. But, star running back Jahmyr Gibbs also didn't practice and was listed with a shoulder injury. Fellow running back Jacob Saylors (neck) was a limited participant. Like Campbell said, Amon-Ra St. Brown sat out with his ankle injury, and Rakestraw was a limited participant. Starting defensive lineman Tyleik Williams also didn't practice due to illness. away.headline: Vikings-Lions First Injury Report
away.blurb: LP = Limited participant in practice. DNP = Did not participate in practice. Probable = the league defines a Probable injury designation as a 75% or greater chance of playing. Historically, 95% of players designated probable are active and played on game day. Questionable = the league defines a Questionable injury designation as being 'uncertain' of whether the player will play or not. This replaces the former definition of having a 50% chance of playing. Historically, 70-75% of players with a Questionable injury designation were active and played on game day. Doubtful = The league defines a Doubtful injury designation to mean the player is unlikely to participate in the game. In practical terms, teams use the designation when a player has less than a 50% chance to suit up, and active game appearances from this designation remain rare. Historically only around 6% of players with a Doubtful designation are active and played on game day. Out = will not play. Players with this designation are not active on game day and league rules prohibit them from playing. For the Lions, Kerby Joseph had his 3-week window to return from the PUP list opened this week, but he is unlikely to play on Sunday. Jahmyr Gibbs and Amon-Ra St. Brown did not practice Wednesday with shoulder and ankle injuries, respectively, which is something to keep an eye on the rest of the week. For the Vikings, Kevin O'Connell didn't seem overly concerned about either Aaron Jones or Joe Huber. Jones is considered day-to-day while Huber sitting out practice on Wednesday was more precautionary than a sign he won't play on Sunday. Brian O'Neill continues to play through a minor knee injury. We'll see how it plays out with injury updates tomorrow and Friday. Last week the Jets lost a hard fought game to the defending AFC champions New England Patriots. That was understandable. Much less understandable was today's 28 – 25 loss at home to the previously winless Miami Dolphins. The Dolphins dominated the action for most of the game, building a two touchdown lead at halftime and maintaining an 11 point lead with less than five minutes remaining in the game before a late Jets touchdown made the score look closer than the game actually was. This loss came against a Dolphins team that had never held a lead at any point in the season prior to today. Today the Dolphins never trailed. It was a humiliating performance by the Jets. The horrendous Jets loss left the Jets with a 2-5 record to start the season, in 3rd place in the AFC East. Now the Jets look to get back on the winning track as they stay home to take on the 3-4 Las Vegas Raiders in East Rutherford, New Jersey next Sunday. The Raiders have lost four straight games after starting the season 3-0. Their latest loss came at the hands of the Los Angeles Rams by a 35 – 21 score. The Raiders' defense has collapsed in their four game losing streak, surrendering 30+ points in each of the four games. With the Raiders making the long trip east for this game and suffering through the early game start, on paper this looks like a get well game for the Jets. However, the way the Jets are playing no game on the schedule should be looked at as an easy win. Let's take a look at the current odds for this game according to FanDuel Sportsbook . The oddsmakers think this game is close to a tossup. The current line has the Jets home favorites by 1.5 points. The game has an over/under of 44.5 points. On the moneyline the Jets are -118 while the Dolphins are +100. Let's see if the Jets can recover from a terrible loss and take care of business at home against the Raiders. J-E-T-S! The Raiders played the Chiefs (30-27), Patriots (45-17), Bills (33-30), and Rams (35-21) over the last four games, all losses. Three of those four games were at home, but now Vegas heads East to New Jersey to take on the Jets. Outside of the wins over the Dolphins and Chargers in Weeks 1 and 2, the Jets have the worst record of any opponent the Raiders have faced. With Kirk Cousins ’ leash starting to shorten as the losses begin to accumulate, this might be a must-win for the Raiders quarterback. Aaron Glenn is on the hot seat, but when hasn’t he been? The Jets’ two-minute drill woes continued, and this staff continues to find ways to lose. New York lost to Miami 28-25 last week as they tried to dig out of 21-7 and 28-17 deficits. The Jets have a lot of young players that have had to step up lately, but boy, have they been impressive. Braelon Allen had 134 total yards (104 rushing), Omar Cooper Jr. posted 5 receptions for 115 yards and a touchdown, plus Mason Taylor scored twice on five catches for 62 yards. The Jets are 1-5 over the last six games and 5-19 since Glenn took over as head coach, tied for the second-worst (Titans are 4-20 since the start of 2025). Quarterback matchup for Jets vs Raiders · Las Vegas : Kirk Cousins – During the Raiders’ four-game losing streak, Cousins had seven passing touchdowns to two interceptions and averaged 304.0 passing yards per game. Despite playing some of the NFL’s best teams and now going on the road to take on the Jets, Cousins may not have an easier matchup just because the Jets have a losing record. The Jets run the eight-most man coverage, and Cousins ranks 32nd in completion percentage (48.5%), 23rd in passer rating (81.0), and 34th in catchable rate (54.6%) versus man coverage. Cousins has also had issues when blitzed. He ranks 30th in completion percentage when blitzed (53.8%) and 31st in catchable ball rate (57.7%). The Jets blitz at the fourth-highest rate (40%), so this could be a tougher matchup for Cousins than most people expect. · New York : Geno Smith – Smith tied a season-high with three touchdown passes against the Dolphins and his second interception. Smith has thrown picks in back-to-back weeks, which has been a concern the past few years. Smith threw a career-high 17 interceptions in 2025 after 15 in 2024. Smith has the ninth-most danger plays on the season, but it hasn’t translated to picks, so maybe he’s just having good luck with turnovers this season. If Allen and/or Hall are out, you can expect Smith to be chucking on Sunday. He’s thrown 30 passes in three straight games, but I’d expect that streak to be broken against the Raiders. Smith’s attempts line is 30.5, and his yards are 220.5. He could fly over those without Hall or Allen. Nacua left Thursday's practice early with the aforementioned calf injury. Head coach Sean McVay on Friday said Nacua "took part in a majority of the practice, left, (and then) got it checked out." McVay also said that "I don't think he (Nacua) knows exactly when it occurred." Cornerback Trent McDuffie (groin) is also listed as questionable. McDuffie did not practice all week. Meanwhile, inside linebacker Nate Landman (concussion) was ruled out, but is "making good progress," McVay said. With Landman out, McVay confirmed Los Angeles will elevate inside linebacker Eric Kendricks from the practice squad. away.headline: NFL Week 7 Injury Report: Raiders' Quay Walker and Rams' Puka Nacua Listed
away.blurb: Las Vegas Raiders linebacker Quay Walker has been downgraded to questionable with a chest injury ahead of Sunday's game against the Los Angeles Rams. The change raises uncertainty about his availability for the Week 7 matchup at Allegiant Stadium. ESPN's Raiders reporter Ryan McFadden reported the downgrade on X on Saturday. Walker had been a full participant in Friday's practice after being limited on Wednesday and Thursday, according to the Raiders' official injury report. The injury report also lists running back Mike Washington Jr. as questionable for Las Vegas with foot and back issues. For Los Angeles, wide receiver Puka Nacua is questionable with a calf injury, while linebacker Nate Landman has been ruled out with a concussion. Walker was limited during the first two practices of the week before completing Friday's session without a game-status designation on the team's published report. The subsequent downgrade means his availability remains uncertain, although the available reporting does not establish whether he experienced a setback or explain the reason for the change. The Raiders host the Rams on Sunday, Oct. 25, with kickoff scheduled for 4:25 p.m. ET. Las Vegas will need to clarify Walker's status before the game, while his questionable designation leaves open the possibility that he could still play. ESPN's Rich Cimini reported the following update: The goal will likely be for Hall to practice fully Friday. If he completes a full practice without limitations, he could have a good chance of returning Sunday. Braelon Allen Will Start if Hall Can't Play Allen has been effective while handling the majority of the carries in Hall's absence. In his last four starts, the former Wisconsin star has recorded at least 14 carries and rushed for at least 60 yards in each game, including multiple 100-yard performances. Last week against the Miami Dolphins , Allen recorded 17 carries for 104 yards and added six receptions for 30 yards. home.headline: New York Jets Add David Bailey, Braelon Allen to Injury Report
home.blurb: The latest addition is star rookie edge rusher David Bailey, who has a groin injury that is keeping him out of practice on Wednesday. Bailey sustained the injury against the Dolphins, but finished the game. Head coach Aaron Glenn said Bailey came to the Jets practice facility on Monday and said his groin injury was still bothering him. Glenn declined to speculate on whether the injury would keep Bailey out of the game against the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday. "We'll see how he operates," the coach said. "We'll see during the week." Bailey did not practice on Wednesday, with Glenn waiting until later in the week to make an official game status designation. Of greater concern may be the absence of defensive tackle T'Vondre Sweat. The biggest player in the NFL, Sweat sustained a knee injury against the Dolphins and is listed as doubtful. Also doubtful for the Raiders game is edge Joseph Ossai, who has an ankle injury. Both are considered week-to-week on availability. Also nursing an ankle is running back Braelon Allen, who ran for more than 100 yards against the Dolphins. He was listed as limited for Wednesday's practice. The Jets' other star running back, Breece Hall, may return against the Raiders after being a game-time no-go against the Dolphins. He has 357 yards since Hall went down in Week 3, and has performed so well that the Jets are trying to scheme a way to have both backs on the field at the same time. picks.headline: 3 bold predictions for the Browns against the Steelers in Week 8
picks.blurb: 3 bold predictions for the Browns against the Steelers in Week 8 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Packers defeat Panthers WNBA Finals: Dream force Game 7 Bears land DT Jeffery Simmons Brewers win World Series Celebrate, Milwaukee! 3 bold predictions for the Browns against the Steelers in Week 8 Jeffrey Olson, Browns Wire Wed, October 28, 2026 at 8:14 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Cleveland Browns are heading into a divisional showdown this weekend against the Pittsburgh Steelers. This is the second time these two will have matched up this year, with the Browns winning the first time around. However, this game feels like it has more riding on it. The winner of this game will sit alone in first place in the AFC North. It's also a chance for Cleveland to take a two-game advantage in division games, which is a critical playoff tiebreaker. What fireworks can we expect in this game? Here are my three bold predictions. Jared Verse gets on the board Aarong Rogers is the most sacked quarterback in NFL history. He would rather eat the ball and take a sack than put the ball in harm's way by throwing a rushed pass that could be intercepted. We saw a taste of that when the Browns sacked Rogers 5 times when they played earlier this year. I'd imagine that the Steelers will change up their game plan after giving up 8 sacks in the last two games as well as the previously mentioned 5 to Cleveland earlier this year. So it could be a new name that gets his opportunity to sack Rogers. Jared Verse does not have a sack yet this season. His production is undeniably down this year, although he has shown flashes of still being a disruptive player. This feels like an opportune time for him to break through and get his first of the season. KC's back-to-back big days KC Concepcion looked great in the Browns win over the Titans last week. He showed the yards-after-catch ability that we knew he had coming out of college. His quickness is a matchup problem, and now that he is adjusting to the speed of the NFL, we might be seeing that more and more. I am betting that the needle is pointing up for Concepcion after his first career 100-yard receiving game last week. So much so that I believe he will repeat that performance and go for over 100 yards again. This first-round pick has all the ability in the world, and we are watching him come into his own before our eyes. Bust out the brooms The Browns have not swept the season series against the Steelers since 1988. This weekend they will have a chance to break that streak, and I believe that they will. Pittsburgh has been a very middle-of-the-road team this year. Their passing game is pedestrian, and they don't do any one thing especially well. They are ripe for the picking. The thing that gives me the most optimism this week is that I believe that the Browns have the coaching advantage. Todd Monken has this team believing in themselves, and we have seen that reflected in several late-game, one-possession wins this season. When push comes to shove, I think Cleveland is just the more mentally tough team right now. away.blurb: Browns Pro Bowler Lands on Injury Report as Key Contributors Return Skip to main content SI.COM The Cleveland Browns seem to be on the mend when the injury report for Sunday’s game against the Tennessee Titans came out. Key contributors are back on the field, but they are still not out of the weeds yet, with one surprising player listed as questionable who can influence the outcome in Nashville. Denzel Ward was listed as questionable with a hand injury on Friday’s report. He was limited at practice on Friday, and the defense needs him to be healthy. Ward is having an incredible season locking down the offense’s top receiver. Another concerning, questionable designation is Quincy Williams with a neck injury. He has been flying around the field in recent weeks, making big hits and causing fumbles. Williams will be key to rushing Cameron Ward and forcing him to make bad decisions leading to errant throws and turnovers. However, Carson Schwesinger is in the lineup and he is so good that he can make up for Williams’ absence should he be out for the game. The defense continues to be hobbled as Grant Delpit is also listed as questionable with a concussion. He left last week’s game early with the injury, but has not been ruled for this week. The Browns’ stagnant rushing game will get a boost as Dylan Sampson has been upgraded to questionable. He suffered an injury in the first game of the season and has been out since. The defensive line gets a major boost with the return of Mason Graham. His injury in Week 4 looked bad, but he avoided the worst-case scenario and is back in the lineup after missing two games. Michael Hall Jr., Kalia Davis, Out Graham will need to be good, as Michael Hall Jr. continues to remain on the injured list and is out again with an ankle injury. Also on the defensive line, Kalia Davis will not play in the game. The defensive line has caused havoc for other quarterbacks and has shut down the running game. Dillon Gabriel, Teven Jenkins, Out Also out is Dillon Gabriel and Teven Jenkins. Gabriel has practiced and the Browns will have to make a decision on his injury designation soon or risk shutting him down for the season. Jenkins is out, but rookie Austin Barber has stepped up and has played well for the offensive line. If a couple of the questionable players can strap it up on Sunday, then the Browns will receive a major boost to help them improve to an AFC North best 5-2. The Titans do not have much to offer on offense, but rookie Carnell Tate is having a solid season with 344 yards, which is only one yard behind Denzel Boston. Todd Monken believes that Ward will play with a finger injury, but advised, “We’ll see”. When Ward is on the field, quarterbacks generally do not even try to throw his way, but quarterback Cameron Ward can be reckless with the football and throw it his way, leading to a crucial turnover. away.headline: Falcons get 2 key defenders back ahead of Week 8 game vs. Bucs
away.blurb: According to ESPN reporter Marc Raimondi , linebacker Divine Deablo and cornerback Billy Bowman Jr. both returned to practice on Thursday. The two standout defenders sat out of Sunday's win over the San Francisco 49ers, but they appear to have a chance to play in Week 8. Deablo has been dealing with a forearm injury, and his absence against the 49ers gave linebacker Kendal Daniels a chance to wear the green dot. The rookie made the most out of his opportunity, leading the Falcons with 11 total tackles and coming away with two fourth-quarter turnovers to ice the win. Nonetheless, Deablo has been an elite inside linebacker when healthy, and his return should only improve Jeff Ulbrich's defense going into Week 8. As for Bowman, the versatile defensive back is dealing with a hamstring injury that he suffered against the Chicago Bears in Week 6. home.headline: Buccaneers’ Emeka Egbuka gets murky injury update for Falcons game
home.blurb: Recently, Buccaneers head coach Todd Bowles was asked about the availability of Egbuka, Luke Goedeke, and Antoine Winfield Jr. for Week 8. However, the head coach revealed that all three players remain questionable . “They're all questionable,” Bowles said. “We're going to see on Wednesday and Thursday what they do, and I'll have a better answer for you.” Egbuka returned to limited practice on Friday ahead of the Panthers matchup, yet he was unable to receive medical clearance in time to play. The latest update leaves Tampa Bay waiting for further clarity on his recovery as the team prepares for its next divisional test. However, Egbuka's recovery from both the concussion and foot injury will ultimately determine whether he can return against Atlanta. Until the Buccaneers provide another update following his upcoming practices, his availability for Week 8 remains uncertain. home.headline: Buccaneers’ Emeka Egbuka among players included in latest injury report before Falcons game
home.blurb: Egbuka was a limited participant in Thursday's practice as he continued to work through the NFL's concussion protocol. One encouraging sign was his return to a regular practice jersey after previously wearing a non-contact one. The development suggests he is making progress, though he still needs medical clearance before returning to game action. The rookie has been out since sustaining a concussion and a foot injury in the Buccaneers' Week 6 loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers . During the fourth quarter, Steelers linebacker Patrick Queen delivered a hit that brought his shoulder into Egbuka's helmet as the receiver tried to make a play on an incomplete pass. The injuries forced him to sit out Tampa Bay's Week 7 win over the Carolina Panthers. His return would give the Buccaneers another important option in their passing game. Before going down, Egbuka had caught 28 passes for 240 yards and two touchdowns, making him a productive contributor to the team's receiving corps. Luke Goedeke missed Thursday's practice with a calf injury, while Kenny Gainwell was limited by a hip issue. Yaya Diaby and Josiah Trotter returned to full participation, as did Baker Mayfield and Antoine Winfield Jr. The Buccaneers will have to wait and see how Egbuka responds as they prepare to host Atlanta at Raymond James Stadium on Sunday. His return to a regular practice jersey is a positive step, but he must still progress through the concussion protocol and receive final medical clearance to suit up on Sunday. picks.headline: Early odds and bold Parker Washington prediction for Colts vs. Jaguars in Week 8
picks.blurb: Early odds and bold Parker Washington prediction for Colts vs. Jaguars in Week 8 Skip to main content News FanSided NFL Sites Even though the Jacksonville Jaguars didn't play in Week 7, they managed to gain ground in the AFC South , as every other team in the division lost. The Jags are back from their break and will have a prime opportunity to keep building their lead when they play the hapless Indianapolis Colts in Week 8. The Colts are 2-5 and currently showing no signs of getting better this season. Heck, they let everyone know that they're punting on the season when they ousted general manager Chris Ballard, who failed to replenish the Indianapolis roster and left it devoid of talent. Following the dismissal of Ballard, Indy has gone on to hold a fire sale, sending All-Pro guard Quenton Nelson to the Seattle Seahawks in return for a 2027 third-round pick and a fifth in 2028 days before the Jaguars game. While the Nelson trade could incentivize the Jags to make a push for defensive tackle DeForest Buckner , they cannot lose sight of the task at hand, which is beating the dreaded divisional foe. And with this in mind, here are the early odds for Week 8 and a bold Parker Washington prediction. The Colts vs. the Jaguars early odds for Week 8 The game will be held at EverBank Stadium, where the Colts have lost 11 consecutive games. Not surprisingly, the Jaguars are a 7.5-point favorite with a moneyline of -395 , via DraftKings. Bet $395 on them to win $100 if they beat Indianapolis for a total payout of $495. The Colts' moneyline sits at +310. Place a wager of $100 and win $310 if they beat Jacksonville for a total payout of $410. The over/under for the game is set at 49.5 points. ** Keep in mind that odds are refreshed periodically, so they can change at any moment. You may also like: 5 Jaguars who need to step up after the bye Bold Parker Washington prediction for the Jaguars vs. the Colts One of the biggest storylines surrounding the Jaguars in the offseason was that they opted not to make a big splash in free agency because they wanted to take care of their homegrown talent. Thus far, they locked up long snapper Ross Matiscik, defensive end Travon Walker, cornerback Montaric Brown, and tight end Brenton Strange, so you could make the case that general manager James Gladstone achieved the goal. That said, Parker Washington is still waiting on an extension. A sixth-round pick in 2023, Washington showed flashed his first two seasons but was stucked behind Christian Kirk. Jacksonville paved the way for him to start when Kirk was traded to the Houston Texans. Right off the bat, Washington became a key contributor on offense, registering 58 receptions for 807 yards with five touchdowns, all career bests, last year. Washington wasted no time picking up where he left off last year, racking up 26 receptions for 416 yards with four touchdowns. The former Penn State Nittany Lion is on pace to register the first 1,000-yard season of his career and should have no trouble getting the top-market contract he's been looking for . Although the Jags reportedly offered Washington $25 million per year before Week 1 , he rejected the offer. It's possible that he's aiming for an annual average of $30 million. Based on his production, he may be able to get it, and he'll have a prime opportunity when he plays the Colts. Already, Washington posted his first 100-yard game of the season against the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 5. He'll get his second one in Week 8 when he registers seven receptions for a monster 140 yards with two touchdowns against Indy. away.headline: Quenton Nelson, Colts were close to a contract extension in the offseason, per report
away.blurb: In return for the All-Pro guard, the Colts received a 2027 third round pick and 2028 fifth round pick from Seattle. News Sports Things To Do Opinion Real Estate Advertise Obituaries eNewspaper Legals COLTS Quenton Nelson, Colts were close to a contract extension in the offseason, per report Cameron Cocquyt Indianapolis Star Oct. 29, 2026, 1:39 p.m. ET The Indianapolis Colts traded guard Quenton Nelson to the Seattle Seahawks following the firing of general manager Chris Ballard. Nelson had reportedly wanted to sign a long-term contract extension to remain with the Colts. In exchange for Nelson, Indianapolis received a 2027 third-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick. After the Indianapolis Colts fired general manger Chris Ballard 10 days ago, it sent a ripple effect down the organization. Coming off a second-half letdown and loss to the then 0-5 Tennessee Titans , it seemed clear that changes were imminent. Tuesday, the Colts traded Quenton Nelson to the Seattle Seahawks , a franchise cornerstone on the offensive line since Indianapolis drafted him with the No. 6 pick in the 2018 NFL Draft . With uncertainty surrounding the future of the organization, rumors began to swirl about trade requests regarding some of the Colts' most important players. ESPN NFL insider Ian Rapoport joined the Pat McAfee show Wednesday and shed some light on Nelson's situation in Indianapolis. "Is that accurate? He wanted to get a deal done with Indianapolis this off-season," McAfee asked Rapoport. "Yeah, that is true." Rapoport replied. "When Chris Ballard was there, I really thought it was going to get done." Nelson didn't sign an extension. He is currently on the final year of a four-year, $80 million contract, his first large-scale extension following his rookie contract. According to Rapoport, it was up to Nelson if he would be spending the next several years with the Colts' organization. "This is a huge bounty for someone in the middle of the season," Rapoport added. "A lot of people wanted this guy that the Seahawks think is like really, really going to help their run game." Since arriving in Indianapolis, Nelson was selected to the Pro Bowl each of his eight seasons and was named an All-Pro in six of those. Just a short time after Nelson's trade, the Colts moved another key piece of the roster in DeForest Buckner , who returns to the organization that drafted him, the San Francisco 49ers . Indianapolis received a 2027 fourth-round pick. With uncertainty surrounding the organization, there is reason to believe the roster moves won't stop here. Nonetheless, it was an offensive pillar that may have set off a revolving door of player personnel in Indianapolis. We may earn a commission when you buy through links on this page. away.headline: Jaguars-Colts Wednesday injury report: It is time to unleash Jalen Huskey
away.blurb: Johnson was the only Jaguar who did not practice Wednesday, which is not a great sign coming off a bye week. Johnson injured his ankle in the Week 6 loss to the Houston Texans in London, and the Jaguars very well may be without their best safety once they kick off against the Indianapolis Colts in Week 8. Limited in practice for the Jaguars were four players: linebacker Jalani Tavai (hamstring), wide receiver Jakobi Meyers (hamstring), long snapper Ross Matiscik (shoulder), and defensive tackle Ruke Orhorhoro. JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- There should be one clear reaction to the Jacksonville Jaguars' first injury report of Week 8: it is time for Jalen Huskey. Huskey, the No. 100 pick in April's NFL Draft, has yet to log a snap on defense and has only been active for one game. But the Jaguars should use this week to push Huskey toward some real playing time considering starting safety Antonio Johnson missed Wednesday's practice with an ankle injury. With second-year safety Caleb Ransaw on injured reserve and not looking close to returning anytime soon, the Jaguars' options at safety while Johnson recovers are starting safety Eric Murray, backup safety Kaevon Merriweather, second-year special teamer Rayuan Lane, or Huskey. The Jaguars leaned toward Merriweather getting playing time over Huskey at previous points, but it is time for the Jaguars to unleash their rookie. Merriweather has played 45 NFL games and has been in the NFL since 2023, so naturally he has more experience than Huskey does just a few months into his NFL career. away.blurb: LP = Limited participant in practice. DNP = Did not participate in practice. Probable = the league defines a Probable injury designation as a 75% or greater chance of playing. Historically, 95% of players designated probable are active and played on game day. Questionable = the league defines a Questionable injury designation as being ‘uncertain’ of whether the player will play or not. This replaces the former definition of having a 50% chance of playing. Historically, 70-75% of players with a Questionable injury designation were active and played on game day. Doubtful = The league defines a Doubtful injury designation to mean the player is unlikely to participate in the game. In practical terms, teams use the designation when a player has less than a 50% chance to suit up, and active game appearances from this designation remain rare. Historically only around 6% of players with a Doubtful designation are active and played on game day. Out = will not play. Players with this designation are not active on game day and league rules prohibit them from playing. For the Vikings, only Jordan Mason has an injury designation, but his questionable designation is a technical one for those coming off of IR. He will play on Sunday. Christian Darrisaw and Harrison Smith had their customary rest days on Friday. For the Colts, a total of seven players have injury designations. The most significant are starting cornerback Sauce Gardner and starting tight end Tyler Warren, both of whom are out, as is wide receiver Anthony Gould. Starting linebacker Bryce Boettcher is questionable, as is his backup C.J. Allen, which could leave them thin at the position. The same is true at cornerback with Sauce Gardner out and Justin Walley questionable. Lastly, punter Rigoberto Sanchez did not practice all week and is listed as questionable. The Colts added a punter to their roster this week in case he can’t go on Sunday. Chargers vs. Rams bold predictions for NFL Week 8 Ben Strauss, ClutchPoints Thu, October 29, 2026 at 9:26 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The NFL teams based in Los Angeles are not having a great first half of the 2026 NFL season. Both the Chargers and Rams combined have three wins on the season headed into Week 8. The Rams are doing all of the heavy lifting here, but even they are having a disappointing season compared to their offseason expectations. It seems a Rams vs. Chargers Super Bowl is not in the cards this season. While both teams have been frustrating, they are in completely different situations ahead of Week 8. The Rams are very much alive in the NFC playoff race, but they need to continue stacking wins to remain competitive. Meanwhile, the Chargers are 0-6 and somehow still think they'll compete by the end of the season. This game means a lot for both teams, but the Rams arguably have much more to lose. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) So which team will come out on top in this one? Here are three bold predictions ahead of this Battle for Los Angeles in Week 8 between the Chargers and Rams. Rams, Chargers combine for more rushing yards than passing yards Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Both LA teams built their teams to have a strong running game. Jim Harbaugh is known for his love of pounding the rock. The Chargers drafted Omarion Hampton and built a massive offensive line for that very reason. As for the Rams, Sean McVay has always leaned heavily on the running game dating back to the Todd Gurley years. That has continued into 2026, as the Rams popularized 13 personnel usage and have taken to a new level this season. But just how committed are they to running the ball? When both teams combine their final stats, this game will feature more rushing yards than passing yards. That sounds like a crazy prediction on the surface. So exactly how bold is this prediction? The Rams average roughly 70 more passing yards than rushing yards per game this season, compared to an 82-yard gap for the Chargers. So it would be quite shocking if both teams overcame this 152-yard difference. If this happens, it may require both defenses to ball out against the pass and allow a handful of explosive runs. This is definitely bold, but crazier things have happened. The Chargers dominate the line of scrimmage on both sides of the ball If the Chargers are going to have a chance to win this game, they'll have to do so in the trenches. The injury situation for both teams makes this look like a strong possibility. Joe Alt is expected to return from injury for this game. One offensive lineman won't magically turn LA's o-line into an elite unit. However, it could do wonders as he still projects as an elite talent at the position. If the Chargers can count on one side of the line protected, they can always pull out some tricks to protect the other side. It is also important to note that the Rams have only managed 10 sacks in seven games played this season. That puts them at 27th in the NFL and only ahead of pitiful defensive teams like the Dolphins, Eagles, and Cowboys. It really shows that Myles Garrett, Kobie Turner, and Poona Ford are injured. Flipping to the other side, the Chargers and Rams look pretty evenly matched in the trenches. The Rams may hold a slight lead, but nothing too crazy. Ultimately, the Chargers' formula for winning this game is predicated on winning the trenches. This is certainly an area where they could gain an advantage. The Chargers will keep Justin Herbert completely clean, not allowing a single sack. Meanwhile, they will sack Matthew Stafford at least twice. That may not be a huge advantage, but it gives the Chargers a fighting chance. Chargers take Rams to overtime, but lose by a field goal Credit: Denny Medley-Imagn Images It is really tempting to predict that the Chargers will get their first win of the season in this spot. But it just seems too far-fetched. Realistically, the Rams and Chargers are in two completely different worlds on offense. The Rams average more total yards per game than any other team, while the Chargers are statistically a bottom five offense. There's no reason to suggest that will change in Week 8. Furthermore, the Rams absolutely must win this game to stay alive in the NFC playoff race. McVay may be willing to pull out all the stops if this game becomes close, and the Chargers would need to be lucky to survive in that situation. But playing for pride is important too, so the Chargers won't go down without a fight. They just don't have the horses to get the job done. Brandon McManus kicks a game-winning field goal in overtime, cementing himself as the Rams' kicker for the rest of the season. Chargers Star Suffers Injury Setback Amid Challenging Season - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL WNBA Finals: Dream force Game 7 Chargers Star Suffers Injury Setback Amid Challenging Season Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads This season has gone from bad to worse for the Los Angeles Chargers, and one of the Bolts' defensive stars may not be around to help right the ship. Safety Derwin James Jr., who's missed the Chargers' last three games with a nagging hamstring injury, now may be headed to injured reserve, head coach Jim Harbaugh told reporters on Wednesday. What's wrong with Derwin James? As detailed by Elliott Teaford of the Orange County Register , the move to place James on IR isn't official yet, but Harbaugh said "it's looking like he may go to IR." Jun 17, 2026; El Segundo, CA, USA; Los Angeles Chargers safety Derwin James (3) during minicamp at The Bolt. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) He'd miss games against the LA Rams, Houston Texans, Baltimore Ravens and New York Jets, but could come back to play against the New England Patriots. It's a devastating blow for a team in desperate need of a spark, particularly given the expectations placed upon James this offseason. The Chargers rewarded James' elite play with a huge contract extension that made him the highest paid safety in the NFL for the second time in his career. Between James' injury and a struggling offense, though, the Chargers are now the last winless team in the NFL. What does Derwin James mean to the Chargers? So far this season, James' stats haven't exactly jumped off the page. In his three games, he had 21 tackles and broke up a pass. Those numbers, though, belie a spectacular resume thus far. That kind of production and experience is impossible to replace, and this Sunday, Matthew Stafford and the Rams might have a field day with the Bolts defense. Considering the Rams are also looking to rebound from a poor start to the year, this battle for LA supremacy might be the defining week for both franchises. home.blurb: As the Los Angeles Rams near the trade deadline , it has become increasingly clear that the team needs a WR3. While they primarily operate out of 13 personnel, the Rams still use three wide receiver sets at a 55.9 percent rate. It’s true that they are set to get Davante Adams back in approximately six weeks. However, they still lack depth behind Puka Nacua should he miss more time due to injury. However, we can’t keep living in a world from two years ago. The Rams and head coach Sean McVay have let everyone know what they think of Atwell and it isn’t as a WR2 or WR3 in the offense. Despite paying Atwell $10 million that was fully guaranteed, Atwell had six receptions total last season. This year, he has three. It’s clear that the Rams see Atwell as nothing more than a vertical clear-out player. That has value in an offense, but it’s also replaceable. While Thomas would fit the need as the Rams’ “X” receiver when Adams is out, his fit becomes a lot more complicated after that. Meanwhile, Downs would fit in the offense alongside Adams and Nacua and may only cost a fourth- or fifth-round pick. Downs may have more of a market as teams look to add a wide receiver. We’ll see if the Rams get involved. For now, the interest appears to exist. RotoWire recently put together an impact index score to quantify how hard teams have been hit with injuries. The Rams ended up with a moderate score of 4.56, ranking ninth in the NFL in injury impact. However, the Rams have had $67.3 million in cap space out due to injury, which is the fifth-most. Davante Adams and Poona Ford have been the biggest contributors to that with Adams’ $28 million cap-hit and Ford’s $11.4 million. 1. Myles Garrett's Rams Return May Have to Wait Until After the Bye To be clear, this is only me speculating. While there had been reports that Garrett would return to practice this week, the Rams opted not to open his practice window . Given that the Rams are in Washington next week, it seems unlikely that Garrett will test his knee on that field. The Rams then play the Arizona Cardinals the following week. The Rams are likely to continue playing it safe. At this point, it’s hard to see Garrett coming back before the bye. If the Rams are without Shelton, it would likely be Beaux Limmer at center. Without Parkinson, the Rams would be limited in what they could do out of 13 personnel. It’s clear the Rams feel Max Klare isn’t ready. Cardona could miss Sunday’s game, especially as the team signed Jake McQuaide to the practice squad this week. Additionally, cornerback Trent McDuffie was limited while Nate Landman and Desjuan Johnson were full participants. There comes a point when the Rams have to stop living in the fallacy that Tutu Atwell and Konata Mumpfield are good enough. home.headline: Report: Rams WR Puka Nacua's injury not believed to be serious
home.blurb: Oct 23 (Field Level Media) - Rams receiver Puka Nacua sustained a calf injury in practice Thursday that is not expected to be serious, NFL Network reported. Per the report, his status is "up in the air" for the Rams (2-4) for Sunday's road game against the Las Vegas Raiders (3-3). Los Angeles head coach Sean McVay is expected to speak to reporters on Friday. The Rams will be without fellow wideout Davante Adams, who was placed on injured reserve earlier in the week with a ruptured hamstring. The other members of the receiver room are Konata Mumpfield, Jordan Whittington, Tutu Atwell, CJ Daniels and Alex Bachman. Nacua, 25, has 37 catches for 417 yards and one touchdown to go with one rushing score in four games this season. He missed two games with a psoas injury. A two-time Pro Bowl selection, Nacua led the NFL with 129 receptions last season and racked up 1,715 receiving yards with 10 touchdowns in 16 games.

home.headline: Chargers Injury Report: No changes from Bolts’ 2nd day of Rams prep
home.blurb: Offensive guard Kayode Awosika (fibula) and wide receiver Brenen Thompson (quad/hamstring) were once again non-participants. There was hope both could return this week, but they’re slated to miss yet another week at this rate. Receivers Ladd McConkey (concussion) and Tre’ Harris (hamstring) were full and limited, respectively. Having Harris back out there will be huge for the offense, but recent history tells us we can’t be confident in McConkey’s return lasting all that long. Cornerback Rodney Shelley is on pace to return from a hamstring injury and the Chargers will need him with fellow corner Deane Leonard still rehabbing a concussion. Veteran Donte Jackson returning to the field would also be huge for the cornerback room that continues to be wiped out by injuries. Normally you want to see some semblance of progression for players with injuries. Unfortunately the Chargers saw zero steps forward across their entire injury report from Wednesday.

Los Angeles Rams have no clear date for Myles Garrett's return McVay has yet to decide whether the Rams will open Garrett's 21-day practice window, which would allow the defensive end to begin working toward a return. Speaking to reporters on October 26, the coach said he needed to consult the team's medical staff before making that call. Early reports suggested he might return after four weeks, but the recovery period later stretched to six weeks or longer. NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported last week that Garrett was likely to return to practice, with a possible Week 8 appearance in the discussion. Opening the practice window would not guarantee an immediate return to games. The Rams would have 21 days to activate Garrett to the 53-man roster or place him on season-ending injured reserve. Until the team makes that move, he cannot play. Other reports have suggested the wait could continue. ESPN's Dan Graziano reported on October 21 that Garrett was likely to miss at least another two or three weeks. That timeline could push his return toward Week 10, with the Rams scheduled to have a bye in Week 11. Los Angeles improved to 3-4 after beating the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 7, but the team has little room for further setbacks. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Pete Prisco reveals all of his Week 8 picks, including the Bills to top the Ravens in a high-scoring game Getty Images Going to the dogs last week turned out to be dog doodoo. I picked every dog against the spread last week and it looked good early, but then it collapsed late with five straight losses, including both prime-time games Sunday and Monday night. I was 8-6 straight up last week and 6-7-1 against the spread. Hey, the spread record was an improvement, which tells you how bad I've been this season. My ATS record this year is 43-61-3, which is a long way from .500. My straight-up record is 62-44-1. So this week, it's back to just picking the games. Forget all dogs. Trying to get to .500 makes me borrow a coaching cliché they all use. One game at a time. One week at a time. Turnaround time. All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET Baltimore Ravens at Buffalo Bills (-3.5) Sunday, 1 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) Lamar Jackson could be back for the Ravens, but how much will his injured ankle impact his ability to move? The Bills are coming off a bye, so they will be rested. Baltimore's defense was bad in the loss to the Bengals last week, but Buffalo's defense has been awful. Look for a shootout here with Josh Allen getting the best of it. Pick: Bills 35, Ravens 30 Tennessee Titans at Cincinnati Bengals (-10.5) The Titans are having major problems on offense, while the Bengals lit up the Ravens last week. Joe Burrow was special in the second half of that game and I think that will carry over here. Look for an offensive explosion from the Bengals as Burrow starts to get into the MVP talk. Pick: Bengals 36, Titans 10 Arizona Cardinals at Dallas Cowboys (-6.5) Sunday, 1 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Cowboys' offense came alive against the Eagles Monday night, especially on the ground, which isn't a good thing for an Arizona defense that is last in the league in scoring. The Dallas offense should roll and the Arizona offense won't be able to keep up. Dallas big — even on a short week. Pick: Cowboys 37, Cardinals 21 Minnesota Vikings at Detroit Lions (-3) The undefeated Vikings face a tough road game here against Detroit. The Lions offense against the Minnesota defense will be a treat to watch. Jared Goff is playing at a high level right now, but Minnesota's defense is the best in the league in terms of scoring. The Vikings offense is limited, but the Detroit defense has had major problems. But they were better last week, which I think carries over. Lions take it. Pick: Lions 23, Vikings 13 Las Vegas Raiders at New York Jets (-1.5) Kirk Cousins stays in as the starter for the Raiders, but teams have blitzed him the past two weeks. That could be a problem here since the Jets are a top-10 team in blitz percentage. The Raiders have struggled to stop opposing offenses, giving up 28.1 points per game, so look for Geno Smith to have success. Jets win it. Pick: Jets 27, Raiders 16 Cleveland Browns at Pittsburgh Steelers (-3.5) This is a big game for the division lead in the AFC North. The Browns beat the Steelers earlier this year, but this will be a bigger challenge on the road. They are also playing consecutive road games, which will be a challenge. Look for Aaron Rodgers to play well as the Steelers take it. Pick: Steelers 24, Browns 20 Atlanta Falcons at Tampa Bay Buccaneers (-2.5) This is suddenly a big game in the NFC South with the Bucs upsetting Carolina last week and the Falcons upsetting the 49ers. The Tampa Bay running game has come alive, but Atlanta is stingy on the ground, giving up 3.8 per rush. That will mean this is a Baker Mayfield game. Tampa Bay gives up 3.5 per rush, which might make for tough going for Bijan Robinson. That's a problem for the Atlanta offense. Tampa Bay wins it. Pick: Bucs 23, Falcons 17 Indianapolis Colts at Jacksonville Jaguars (-9.5) The Colts are a mess; they are playing consecutive road games, and they haven't won at Jacksonville since 2014, when Andrew Luck was the quarterback. Oh, and they traded their best offensive lineman, Quentin Nelson. The Jaguars are coming off a bye, so they will be rested. This one will get ugly as the Jaguars bounce back from the loss to the Texans in London. Pick: Jaguars 30, Colts 16 Los Angeles Chargers (+6.5) at Los Angeles Rams Sunday, 4:05 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The battle of Los Angeles isn't quite the game many expected before the season. The Chargers, coming off a bye, haven't won yet and the Rams have been a disappointment. But the Rams won last week at Las Vegas to seemingly right things. They will win here, but the rested Chargers will keep it close. Pick: Rams 23, Chargers 20 Kansas City Chiefs (-1.5) at Denver Broncos Sunday, 4:25 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) The Chiefs' offense was lifeless in Seattle on Sunday night and now faces a tough Denver defense. They have to find ways to get the running game going again with Kenneth Walker. Bo Nix showed some life last week in the victory over Arizona, but this Chiefs defense will be a challenge. Look for a low-scoring game won by Kansas City, with Walker getting going against Denver's defense, which gives up 4.6 yards per rush. Pick: Chiefs 19, Broncos 14 New England Patriots (-7) at Miami Dolphins The Dolphins won their first game last week and have been in a lot of their losses. But this New England team will be a challenge, even at home. The Patriots are coming off a bad road loss to the Bears, and they will be rested, having played on Thursday. The defense limits the Dolphins' offense, and Drake Maye will play well. New England wins it. Pick: Pats 28, Dolphins 14 Philadelphia Eagles at Washington Commanders (-5.5) Sunday, 8:20 p.m. on NBC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) This might be an elimination game of sorts for these two. Both need a victory in the worst way — even in their horrible division. The Eagles are crippled by injuries, but Washington has plenty of their own. With the Eagles on a short week off a Monday night game and the Commanders off a bye, Washington will win it. Pick: Commanders 28, Eagles 16 Chicago Bears at Seattle Seahawks (-3) Monday, 8:15 p.m. on ESPN, ABC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Bears are riding high behind Caleb Williams and an improved defense. But this is a tough road trip against a Seattle team that showed what it can do on defense by shutting down the Chiefs Sunday night. Seattle also got the running game going. The Seattle defense will slow down the Chicago offense, and the Seahawks will win it. Pick: Seahawks 24, Bears 17 Carolina Panthers at Green Bay Packers (-3.5) Thursday, 8:15 p.m. on Amazon Prime These two are both coming off losses. The Carolina loss featured the Bucs running over them for 258 rushing yards. It's been a problem all year. But the Packers don't run it very well, so something has to give. Carolina gave Jordan Love fits last year, but that will change here. Carolina gives up 27.7 points per game. Love lights them up and Josh Jacobs gets the run game going. picks.blurb: Week 8 NFL picks against the spread, predictions for every game: Chiefs look to bounce back vs. Broncos - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Packers defeat Panthers WNBA Finals: Dream force Game 7 Bears land DT Jeffery Simmons Brewers win World Series Celebrate, Milwaukee! Frank Schwab Senior writer Thu, October 29, 2026 at 3:49 PM UTC · 7 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads For the Denver Broncos, Week 1 had to feel like a bad flashback. The first 12 times that Patrick Mahomes started against the Broncos, the Kansas City Chiefs won every time. Then there was a shift with Sean Payton in charge, and the Broncos won two of three against Mahomes and the Chiefs. The 2026 season opener, though, was like old times. It wasn't Mahomes that ruined the Broncos in the opener, though he played pretty well. It was Kenneth Walker III doing most of the damage, as he ran through many Denver missed tackles for 173 rushing yards. Also, the Chiefs' defense shut down Denver in a 31-10 win. It was a complete, impressive performance. It doesn't seem like much has changed since then. The Chiefs started 5-0 before losing last week at Seattle, a very tough opponent. The Broncos are 5-2 but questions persist about their offense. While the defense on the whole has been better for the Broncos, the run defense isn't great. Denver is 26th in EPA ( expected points added ) per rush allowed. It's easy to say that the Seahawks showed everyone how to beat the Chiefs — take Walker out of the game — but not everyone has Seattle's defense to pull that off. The Broncos showed once they aren't a great matchup against Walker. That's a big reason Kansas City -1.5 is the pick. We saw in the season opener that the Chiefs' dominance over the Broncos might not be over. Kansas City Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III had 173 rushing yards in Week 1 against the Broncos. (AP Photo/Colin E. Braley) Here are the rest of the picks against the spread for Week 8 of the NFL season: Panthers (+3.5) over Packers There's no way the Panthers are as bad as they played last week, when they were down 33-6 to the Buccaneers by halftime. Competent teams that get embarrassed usually bounce back well. The Packers are still a tough team to predict. Raiders (+1.5) over Jets The early East Coast start has been death for the Raiders for a long time, but they are probably the better team. They are certainly the better coached team. The Raiders are on a four-game losing streak but look at the opponents: Chiefs, Patriots, Bills, Rams. Those are four of the strongest teams in the NFL. If Las Vegas can't win here, it might be Fernando Mendoza time. Cowboys (-6.5) over Cardinals The Cowboys are going to score. The Cardinals have given up at least 30 points in six of their eight games. Dallas showed on Monday night that its offense is back, but what about the defense? Maybe a strong fourth quarter against the Eagles is a sign that the Cowboys' defense can be somewhat competent. It's scary to pick the Dallas laying points to anyone because they'll need to get stops, but it would be a surprise if they don't score 30. Buccaneers (-2.5) over Falcons Good luck figuring out either of these teams. The Buccaneers could be better than we think. Their only significant weakness has been pass offense, and that is explained by having an undrafted rookie starting three of their seven games. We don't know if Baker Mayfield is fully healthy, considering he had just 11 pass attempts in his return from a dislocated right thumb last week, but if he is maybe the Bucs can get on a roll. Browns (+3.5) over Steelers Teams coming back from an international game and playing right away without a bye are 0-3-1 this season. The losses were by 12, 11, and 6 points, and the close loss was by the Texans as a 10-point favorite last week. The tie was the Commanders when they were favored at home against the Giants. It's a hard turnaround, and it's what the Steelers face coming back from Paris last Sunday. Both of these teams are 5-2 but flawed, and I'll ride with the angle of the Browns not being the team that played in France last week. Jaguars (-9.5) over Colts It's hard to imagine being a Colts player this week. Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner were traded and everyone else with any value has to wonder if they're next. It's actually surprising the line is less than 10 points against a Jaguars team coming off a bye and a loss. This one could get really ugly. The remainder of the Colts' season could get really ugly. Ravens (+3.5) over Bills You've seen this here before: This all depends on if Lamar Jackson plays. This week, I assume he will. It seemed like he was close last week and he practiced in full on Wednesday. There would be some real frustration if he's not back for this game, which Baltimore might need to win to start to save its season. The Ravens' remaining schedule is the toughest in the NFL, according to DVOA . If he does play, we know the Bills defense is not very good. Getting more than a field goal seems good. Vikings (+3.5) over Lions If the Vikings' build was reversed, and they had a fun offense that was clearly one of the two best in the sport but a defense that was unreliable and among the 10 worst in the NFL, we'd respect them more. How do we know that? The 2026 Buffalo Bills, that's how. Minnesota's defense has been remarkable. Look at the Chicago Bears this season. In three of Caleb Williams' four starts, Chicago is averaging 39 points. In the other start, against the Vikings, the Bears scored three points at home (Williams got injured in that game but not until the middle of the fourth quarter). Maybe Detroit will figure out Brian Flores' defense, but nobody else has and I'm willing to take more than a field goal with the Vikings. Titans (+10.5) over Bengals The Titans have been blown out only twice. They lost by 13 to the Jets in Week 1 and 23 to the Texans in Week 5. Every other game has been decided by six or fewer points. The Titans have won only one of those games, but they're keeping it close. It's possible Joe Burrow will add to his growing MVP argument and torch Tennessee in a blowout, but this seems like a good spot for an ugly underdog. Rams (-6.5) over Chargers Typically, an 0-6 team coming off a bye would be a fine choice. The Chargers don't want to get embarrassed all season, but they're simply not a good team in any phase. That is shocking but also irrefutable. This is the exact type of contrarian pick I'd like to make but I just can't get there with the Chargers. Patriots (-7) over Dolphins It's possible the Dolphins get some confidence from their first win. It's also possible they let down a bit: It's still a 1-5 team whose goal was to get that first win out of the way. On the other side, there's a Patriots team coming off a loss with three extra days of rest. Commanders (-5.5) over Eagles A low point of this week was looking at the schedule and realizing this was the Sunday night game. Not fun. Not sure what's more surprising: That a 1-4-1 Commanders team is a 5.5-point favorite over the Eagles, or that the Commanders are the pick. The Eagles' best remaining effort was going to come on a Monday night against the rival Cowboys, and that effort was pretty meager. It won't get better. Bears (+3) over Seahawks The Sunday night game might not be good, but Monday night makes up for it. This one is fun (and should have been the Week 1 opener, but that's an old gripe). If there's an offensive coach that can figure out the Seahawks' defense, it's Ben Johnson. Caleb Williams has been on a heater since returning from a hamstring injury. Bet on the Chicago Bears to cover the spread on Monday night at sportsbooks On the other side, Seattle's offense will be happy to see the Bears defense after a tough stretch of opposing defenses, and perhaps Jaxon Smith-Njigba goes wild. It should be a good game, and if that holds true it'll be nice to have the underdog. Last week : 5-8-1 Season to date: 46-58-2

Broncos vs Chiefs preview: Denver attempts a redo KANSAS CITY, MO - SEPTEMBER 14: Bo Nix #10 of the Denver Broncos reacts after a play against the Kansas City Chiefs during the second half of an NFL football game at Arrowhead Stadium on September 14, 2026 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images Ian St. Clair Wed, October 28, 2026 at 11:00 AM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The first game of the 2026 season for your Denver Broncos did not go according to plan. Not that anyone in Broncos Country needs a reminder. Denver was flogged 31-10 by the Kansas City Chiefs. And the Broncos defense still hasn't tackled Kenneth Walker. Thankfully, and hopefully, Denver gets a crack at a redo this Sunday in Denver. A win at home against Patrick Mahomes, Walker, and Kansas City would give the Broncos the lead in the AFC West. FanDuel Sportsbook has Denver as the home underdog at +1.5 points, though that's basically a pick 'em at this point. The total sits over/under 40.5 points, with a lean toward the over at -115. Offensive Rankings Kansas City : Sixth in total offense (380.5 yards per game), fifth in rushing offense (141.5 YPG), 11th in passing offense (239.0 YPG), 14th in scoring offense (23.8 points per game). Denver : Thirtieth in total offense (270.0 yards per game), 24th in rushing offense (94.9 YPG), 27th in passing offense (175.1 YPG), tied for 24th in scoring offense (20.6 points per game). Defensive Rankings Kansas City : Fourteenth in total defense (323.3 yards per game), 13th in rushing defense (99.5 YPG), 17th in passing defense (223.8 YPG), second in scoring defense (17.2 points per game). Denver : Twenty-third in total defense (349.0 yards per game), 28th in rushing defense (133.3 YPG), 12th in passing defense (215.7 YPG), seventh in scoring defense (20.1 points per game). Here are the MHR staff's keys to Sunday's game. Win the turnover battle As we saw in the Thursday night win over the Seattle Seahawks, when the Broncos defense creates turnovers and the offense protects the ball, Denver wins. The Broncos have been better at creating takeaways this season, and they need to carry that over on Sunday. Force Mahomes into some rushed throws and/or punch the ball out to give Bo Nix and the offense some added possessions. On top of that, Nix and the offense need to continue to protect the ball. Win the turnover battle on Sunday, and the Broncos put themselves in a great spot to win the game. — Ian St. Clair Stop the Chiefs run game Mahomes is continuing to play based off who he was two years ago and not putting in the effort to stay great. I like our chances if we force him to throw on our excellent secondary. Stop Kenneth Walker and win the game. — Sadaraine Tackle Kenneth Walker III The Broncos were hanging tough in the first half in that Week 1 matchup, but the horrific tackling eventually led to big plays in the run game. The Chiefs ran away from Denver in the second half. We all remember how much we overreacted to that first game, but man, did they miss too many tackles to count, and the overreaction was warranted. Since then, however, the Broncos defense has been pretty damn good and the offense is finally waking up. Keep up that momentum, and they should take care of business this weekend. — Tim Lynch Feed Jonah Coleman No need to get cute. Let Jonah Coleman build off the game he had against the Arizona Cardinals. Commit to the running attack. Get the young guys involved. Coleman and RJ Harvey had great games in Phoenix. Keep that going. The passing attack will open up once teams are forced to respect the run. — Adam Malnati Score more points than KC Using advanced analytics, the keys to this game are simple. When the Broncos score fewer points than their opponent, they are 0-2, and when they score more, they are 5-0. Further proving this point, they are 0-1 vs. the Chiefs this season when scoring fewer points than them. However, they were 2-0 against the Chiefs last season when they scored more points than their division rivals. So, according to these advanced analytics, if they can score more points than the Chiefs in this game, they will be 6-2. — Scotty Payne What are your keys to Sunday's game?

Chiefs vs. Broncos Preview: AFC West Rivals Prepare for Crucial Showdown Photo by: Joe Camporeale Stephan Stroud Thu, October 29, 2026 at 8:28 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Kansas City Chiefs will travel to Denver on Sunday for a crucial AFC West matchup against the Broncos. With Kansas City sitting at 5-1 and Denver at 5-2, both teams have plenty at stake as they look to strengthen their position in the division race. The game is scheduled for 4:25 p.m. ET at Empower Field at Mile High and will air on CBS. The Broncos enter with momentum after winning three consecutive games, while the Chiefs are looking to bounce back from their first loss of the season. Chiefs Look to Bounce Back Head coach Andy Reid and quarterback Patrick Mahomes will try to get Kansas City back on track after a disappointing 20-3 loss to the Seattle Seahawks. The Chiefs struggled to generate offense, finishing with just 213 total yards and failing to reach the red zone. Mahomes threw for 165 yards and an interception in the defeat. He will need a stronger performance against a Denver defense that has consistently pressured opposing quarterbacks this season. Running back Kenneth Walker III could be a major factor after dominating the Broncos in the teams' first meeting. Walker rushed for 173 yards and a touchdown in Kansas City's 31-10 victory in September. If the Chiefs can establish their ground game again, it could open opportunities for Mahomes and the passing attack. Broncos Aim to Protect Home Field Denver head coach Sean Payton will look to keep his team's winning streak alive behind quarterback Bo Nix. The second-year quarterback has shown his ability to make plays with both his arm and legs, and he delivered an impressive performance in the Broncos' 30-16 win over Arizona. Nix threw for 222 yards and added 73 rushing yards, including a 62 yard touchdown run. His mobility could be important against a Kansas City defense that will try to disrupt Denver's offensive rhythm. The Broncos' defense will also be key. Led by pass rushers Nik Bonitto and Zach Allen, Denver has the ability to pressure Mahomes and force mistakes. Cornerback Pat Surtain II's improved injury status could provide a boost to the secondary, although Denver's final injury report will be worth monitoring. What to Watch For The biggest matchup will be Kansas City's offense against Denver's pass rush. If the Broncos consistently pressure Mahomes, they could make life difficult for the Chiefs. However, Kansas City's experience and offensive talent make the visitors dangerous in any close game.

Live Simms Unbuttoned Brian Hamilton , Brian Hamilton Sunday’s AFC West showdown in Denver carries real divisional weight, with the Kansas City Chiefs (5-1) holding a half-game lead over the Broncos (5-2). Kansas City is coming off its first loss of the season, while Denver has won three straight and can move ahead of the Chiefs in the division with a victory. The teams met in the season opener on September 14 at Arrowhead Stadium. The Chiefs rolled to a 31-10 win, outgaining Denver 392 yards – 176 yards. Patrick Mahomes threw two touchdown passes and ran for another score, but the star of the night was offseason addition Kenneth Walker III who gashed Denver for 173 rushing yards and a touchdown on 23 carries. The Chiefs arrive in Denver looking to rebound from their 20-3 loss at Seattle last weekend, a game in which they were simply outclassed as Mahomes and co. never found a rhythm. Kansas City managed only 213 total yards and 11 first downs and failed to reach the red zone, while Mahomes completed 19 of 33 passes for 165 yards with no touchdowns and an interception. Walker, facing his former team, was held to just 36 yards on 14 carries after entering the night averaging a league-leading 133 rushing yards per game. Seattle controlled the ball for nearly 36 minutes, converted 11 of 16 third downs and got 150 receiving yards and a touchdown from Jaxon Smith-Njigba . Even when Kansas City had chances to get back into the game, Harrison Butker missed field goals from 58 and 45 yards, leaving the Chiefs with only a third-quarter field goal. Denver, meanwhile, enters with momentum after a 30-16 road win over Arizona. Bo Nix supplied the game’s biggest play with a career-long 62-yard touchdown run late in the second quarter and finished with 222 passing yards and 73 rushing yards, while RJ Harvey turned a screen pass into a 52-yard touchdown and J.K. Dobbins added a one-yard score. The Broncos’ defense repeatedly disrupted Jacoby Brissette and the Cardinals’ offense, producing 12 quarterback hits, six tackles for loss and three sacks. Kansas City owns a 74-59 all-time advantage and dominated Denver with a 16-game winning streak from 2015 through 2023, including Mahomes winning his first 12 starts against the Broncos. Denver finally broke that run in 2023 and has since shown it can compete with KC, but the Chiefs reasserted themselves emphatically with September’s 31-10 victory. The winner Sunday takes the reigns in the AFC West as we move into the second half of the season. away.blurb: The distinction is that Simmons’ absence is not new. Undrafted rookie Kahlil Benson will continue at left tackle, while Joshua Ezeudu is expected to replace Moore on the right side against Seattle. The concern is the combined exposure at both edges. Patriots vs. Dolphins bold predictions for AFC East clash in NFL Week 8 Steve Silverman, ClutchPoints Fri, October 30, 2026 at 5:29 AM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The New England Patriots will be a rested and motivated team when they take the field in South Florida to take on the Miami Dolphins . The Patriots lost a hard-fought game against the Chicago Bears last Thursday night, but the defeat was a competitive effort that demonstrated they could play on the road against a team with legitimate Super Bowl aspirations. The assignment this week doesn't compare. The Dolphins lack the kind of talent on either side of the ball to put up a 60-minute fight against QB Drake Maye and a motivated Patriots team. Miami earned its first victory of the season in their Week 7 game against the New York Jets, but they benefitted greatly from an inefficient and sloppy game from the Jets. Patriots feeling good about their consistent level of play It is unlikely that the Patriots will come at them in a similar manner. New England has played four consecutive solid games, and three of them were victories. When they took down the Buffalo Bills on the road in Week 4, it demonstrated that Mike Vrabel 's team was back on track and was ready to make a run at the AFC East title once again. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) They are 1.5 games behind the first-place Bills, so they have quite a lot of work to do to get there. However, they have more than enough focus and talent to get past the Dolphins on the road. As the Patriots prepare for this game , they are fairly confident that their offense is on the right track. Mike Vrabel would like to see his defense pick up its level of play and start to force more turnovers. If New England can assert itself on the defensive side and take the ball away from its opponents, they are going to put games away much earlier in the second half and avoid the tension that comes with a game that goes down to the wire. That's what should happen in this game. Maye will throw for 275 yards and 2 TDs against Dolphins The Patriots will not look at this game as one they will win by merely showing up. Throughout the years, playing the Dolphins on the road has often been a chore that has regularly been unpleasant for the visitors. Even in the prime years of Tom Brady's leadership, the Patriots have regularly been pushed hard by the Dolphins. The Patriots are 17-40 all-time in games played in Miami. Maye will not take the Dolphins lightly. He should be close to his best because he appears to have overcome the poor start he had in early season games in Seattle and Jacksonville. Maye has risen quite a bit in the ranks of NFL quarterbacks after his early struggles. He has completed 141 of 214 passes for 1,784 yards with 13 TDs and 8 interceptions. Maye's ability to get away from the pass rush is a big part of his game. He has run for 211 yards and 2 TDs, but the most important part of his athleticism is his ability to get away from the pass rush and get the ball to his receivers. It seems very unlikely that the Dolphins secondary is going to stop tight end Hunter Henry along with wideouts Romeo Doubs and DeMario Douglas. The big question revolves around A.J. Brown. He has been limited by injuries this season and has played just three game and has caught just 9 passes for 101 yards. He may or may not be ready to contribute to the Patriots' effort in this game because his knee appears to have flared up. However, the Patriots are expecting him to become their go-to receiver at one point this season. Malik Willis will throw for 150 yards, but toss two interceptions Mandatory Credit: Robert Deutsch-Imagn Images Vrabel wants to see his defense step up quite a bit in the weeks to come. When the Patriots made their charge last season, Maye and the offense got a big assist from the defense as it stepped up by forcing takeaways. The Pats are going to attempt to do this by putting pressure on QB Malik Willis. The former Packer has tried to keep the Dolphins afloat, but the Dolphins have just one win this season. Willis has completed 87 of 151 passes for 1,057 yards with a 4-4 TD-interception ratio. He has also rushed for 223 yards and 3 TDs. Willis has been sacked 16 times this season, and linebacker Elijah Ponder of the Patriots will be after him. Ponder leads New England with 5.5 sacks and should get at least 1.5 in this game. Willis will be trying to get the ball to Malik Washington. He leads the Dolphins with 26 receptions for 289 yards but he has yet to find the end zone. Bold game prediction: Patriots 33, Dolphins 13 The Patriots have too much talent and they are focused on playing consistent, error-free football from this point forward. While many Patriots teams have had problems on the road against the Dolphins, this team will not. Look for Maye and RB Rhamondre Stevenson to get the Patriots off to a good start, and the defense will keep the Dolphins from mounting a charge. The Patriots will have control of this game prior to the end of the third quarter and New England will gain its fourth win in five games. Dolphins (1-5) team that earned its first win of the season last week. The Patriots average 22.9 points per game compared with Miami’s 16.3. New England’s three-game winning streak ended in a 30-24 loss at Chicago last Thursday, despite Drake Maye completing 24 of 31 passes for 321 yards and two touchdowns while also rushing for a score. The loss can be attributed to a costly interception from Maye in the red zone in the second quarter and New England compounded it with 10 penalties and a defense that missed 16 tackles. Miami, meanwhile, is coming off its best afternoon of the season, a 28-25 road victory over the Jets on October 25 that gave coach Jeff Hafley his first win and kept the Dolphins from starting 0-6. Malik Willis was the catalyst, completing 14 of 21 passes for 208 yards and two touchdowns to rookie Caleb Douglas , adding 37 rushing yards and another score, and converting a game-clinching fourth-and-1 in the final two minutes. Miami scored touchdowns on three of its first four possessions and led 21-7 at halftime before a late Jets comeback made things interesting. Ollie Gordon II rushed for 103 yards and a touchdown, while Douglas’ 63-yard fourth-quarter catch-and-run provided the winning points. This rivalry has swung toward New England recently after several seasons in which Miami consistently gave the Patriots problems. The teams’ most recent meeting came January 4, 2026, when New England completed a season sweep with a dominant 38-10 victory at Gillette Stadium to finish the 2025 regular season 14-3. Rhamondre Stevenson was the centerpiece, rushing seven times for 131 yards and two touchdowns and catching another touchdown from Maye, while TreVeyon Henderson added two rushing scores; Maye finished 14 of 18 for 191 yards and a touchdown before exiting early in the fourth quarter. New England outgained Miami 457-180. That capped the Patriots’ first season sweep of Miami since 2016.
