New England Patriots Media Relations WEEK 8 · Sun 11/01 · 4:25 PM EST New England Patriots Miami Dolphins PATRIOTS: Game Release (PDF) | Roster | Depth Chart | Stats DOLPHINS: Roster | Depth Chart | Stats | Roster Flip Card (PDF) The New England Patriots will be on the road for the second straight week when they travel to face the Miami Dolphins in the first of two 2026 meetings. The Dolphins will play at Gillette Stadium in the second game to close out the 2026 regular season. The date and time for that game have not been announced yet. Last season, the Patriots swept the series with a 33-27 win at Miami (9/14) and a 38-10 win to close out the 2025 regular season at Gillette Stadium (1/4). The Patriots will look to win their third straight game over the Dolphins and go 3-0 in the AFC East. Related Links How to Watch and Stream Sunday's Patriots Game Against the Dolphins | NFL Week 8 SERIES HISTORY The New England Patriots earned their 11th series sweep and first since the 2016 season last year with a 33-27 win at Miami (9/14) and a 38-10 win in the rematch in the final game of the season (1/4). The Patriots and Dolphins will meet for the second time in 2026 in the regular season finale at Gillette Stadium in a game that is not scheduled at this time. It will be the 19th time that the two teams will square off in the final game of the year and the second straight year that the Patriots will host the game. Nine of those final games have been played in New England with the Patriots holding a 5-4 edge in those games. Overall, the Patriots are 9-8 when facing Miami in the final game of the year. New England has the advantage against Miami in home games, leading the series 39-21 - including 18-6 at Gillette Stadium - but are 18-43 when playing on the road against Miami. The Dolphins and Patriots met for the first time in 1966 and began playing twice a year during the 1967 regular season, except in 1982 during a players' strike. The two teams have played three times in the postseason with New England holding a 2-1 advantage. Photo by Eric J. WHAT TO LOOK FOR A Patriots win would extend their streak to three straight wins against the Dolphins following their series sweep of Miami last season, their 11th between the division rivals. A Patriots win would give them a 3-0 record against AFC East opponents after a 29-26 win at Buffalo on Oct. 4 and a 26-19 win vs. the New York Jets on Oct. 18. In 2025, the Patriots started the year with a 3-0 record in the division. The Patriots scored more than 30 points in both wins against Miami last year with a 33-27 win at Miami on Sept. 14 and a 38-10 win at Gillette Stadium on Jan. 4, 2026. The Patriots have scored 30 points or more in both games against Miami six total times (1967, 1986, 2010, 2016, 2018 and 2025). PATRIOTS TO WATCH Weight: 249 lbs College: Arkansas TE Hunter Henry enters this week tied with Russ Francis with 28 touchdowns and needs 1 to move into sole possession of third place on the team's all-time list for touchdowns among tight ends. Rhamondre Stevenson Weight: 227 lbs College: Oklahoma RB Rhamondre Stevenson joined Jim Nance (45), Sam Cunningham (43), Corey Dillon (37), Steve Grogan (35), LeGarrette Blount (34), Tony Collins (32) and Curtis Martin (32) as the only Patriots players with 30 career rushing touchdowns after he scored on a 5-yard run in the first quarter against Las Vegas. He needs 2 rushing touchdowns to tie Curtis Martin and Tony Collins for sixth place on the Patriots alltime list for rushing touchdowns. He has had 2 rushing touchdowns in a game six times, with the last coming in the 2025 season-finale vs. Miami on Jan. 4, 2026. Stevenson has 206 career receptions and joined Kevin Faulk (431), James White (381), Tony Collins (261) and Sam Cunningham (210) as the only New England running backs with 200 receptions. He needs 4 receptions to tie Sam Cunningham for fourth place among all Patriots running backs in career receptions. Stevenson (3,954) needs 46 yards to join Sam Cunningham (5,453), Jim Nance (5,323) and Tony Collins (4,647) as the only Patriots players to reach 4,000 rushing yards. Stevenson had a career-high 93 yards receiving last week at Chicago. If he registers at least 90 yards receiving this week, he will become just the second Patriots running back with back-to-back games with at least 90 yards receiving. RB Ron Burton had 94 yards receiving at Houston on Nov. 18, 1962 and followed that performance with 97 yards receiving on Nov. 23, 1962 vs. Buffalo. Stevenson enters this week in 22nd place on the Patriots all-time scoring list with 220 points. With a touchdown this week at Miami, he will move ahead of Wes Welker (225) and tie Curtis Martin (226) for 20th on the team's all-time list. Weight: 225 lbs College: North Carolina QB Drake Maye completed a 48-yard touchdown pass to RB Rhamondre Stevenson at the end of the second quarter last week at Chicago for his 11th touchdown of at least 30 yards over the last two seasons. He then threw a 30-yard touchdown pass to TE Eli Raridon in the third quarter for his 12th, the most in the NFL over that span. Josh Allen and Jalen Hurts each have nine touchdowns of at least 30 yards over the last two seasons. It is Maye's second 40-yard touchdown pass of the 2026 season. He had a 42-yard touchdown pass to WR Romeo Doubs vs. the New York Jets on Oct. 18, 2026. Maye has had two games this year with 2 touchdown passes of at least 30 yards. In addition to the two at Chicago, he also had a 35- yard touchdown pass to WR DeMario Douglas and a 34-yard touchdown pass to WR Kyle Williams in the win vs. Las Vegas on Oct. 11, 2026. He also had two 30-yard touchdown passes on Oct. 13, 2024 vs. Houston with a 40-yard touchdown pass and 35-yard touchdown pass. If Maye has one more game this season with at least two 30- yard touchdown passes, he will match the team record for the most games with at least two 30-yard touchdown passes in a game with three such games, set by Steve Grogan (1979 and 1983) and Tom Brady (2007 and 2009). If Maye throws 2 touchdowns of at least 30 yards this week at Miami, he will join Tom Brady (2009 - Oct. 18 vs. Tennessee and Oct. 25 at Tampa Bay; 2007 - Oct. 14 at Dallas and Oct. 21 at Miami) and Mike Taliaferro (1969 - Nov. 23 vs. Buffalo and Nov. 30 at Miami) as the only Patriots quarterbacks to throw two 30-yard touchdown passes in consecutive games. Maye has gone four straight games with at least 2 touchdown passes. Maye had a streak of five straight games with at least 2 touchdown passes last season. The Patriots record for most consecutive games in a season with at least 2 touchdown passes is 10 by Tom Brady in 2007 and 2014. Maye threw for 321 yards last week against Chicago. If he throws for 300 yards this week against Miami, he will be the first Patriots quarterback with back-to-back 300-yard games since Tom Brady in 2019 when he threw for 348 yards at Washington (10/6) and 334 yards vs. the New York Giants (10/10). Christian Elliss Weight: 231 lbs College: Idaho LB Christian Elliss tied a career-high with 13 total tackles last week at Chicago. He also had 13 total tackles vs. Buffalo on Jan. 5, 2025. The last Patriots player to reach 10 or more tackles in back-to-back games was LB Robert Spillane in 2025 with 15 tackles vs. Pittsburgh (9/21) and 10 vs. Carolina (9/28). Darius Muasau Weight: 230 lbs College: UCLA LB Darius Muasau leads the team with 8 special teams tackles and needs 2 this week to reach 10 total special teams tackles. Last season, the Patriots had four players reach double digit special teams tackles with LB Christian Elliss (18), S Brenden Schooler (14), LB Marte Mapu (12) and LB Jack Gibbens (10). Muasau has three games in 2026 with 2 special teams tackles: at Buffalo (10/4), vs. Las Vegas (10/11) and at Chicago (10/22). Since 2000, the team record for the most games with at least 2 special teams tackles is eight games by LB Larry Izzo in 2004. It's been a largely disappointing first half of the season for wide receiver A.J. Brown in his debut campaign with the New England Patriots . Things are possibly about to get worse for the Patriots and their marquee offseason trade acquisition. New England could potentially afford to sit Brown in Week 8 if he's not healthy enough, as the Patriots are heavy road favorites for Sunday's contest versus the Miami Dolphins. New England has a pair of NFC North contenders on deck in Weeks 9 and 10 with the Green Bay Packers and Detroit Lions, respectively, before its Week 11 bye. The Patriots are just 4-3 this fall, however, so if they want to make a run at their second straight AFC East crown and put pressure on the Buffalo Bills (5-1), they can't take the Dolphins for granted. Brown has played in just three of New England's first seven contests this year as he missed Weeks 2, 3, 4 and 5 due to a high-ankle sprain. The three-time Pro Bowler returned to action in Week 6 against the New York Jets but has yet to have an impact on offense. Brown has played only 132 offensive snaps in his three games and has recorded nine catches for 101 scoreless yards on 20 targets. His longest reception of the season has gone for just 18 yards, but Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel said on Monday that he isn't concerned about the 29-year-old's lack of production. Thursday's news still leaves the door open for Brown to take the field and perhaps turn things around on Sunday, but it's not looking great.

home.blurb: Based on the NFL's five-step Return to Play protocol, Proctor still has to go through "non-contact training drills" and then "full football activity involving contact." The final injury report will come out Friday and at this time it would be a surprise if Proctor weren't ruled out. After being limited in practice because of an ankle injury Wednesday, Brown sat out Thursday and now also is dealing with a knee issue. After sitting out practice Wednesday, he was back at practice Thursday, albeit on a limited basis. The injury report again eight other players listed as limited participants. The other five players listed as limited were TE Greg Dulcich (ankle), S Michael Taaffe (neck/foot), S Dante Trader Jr. (shoulder), WR Malik Washington (knee) and WR Jared Wayne (knee). Besides Brown, the one change on the Patriots injury report involved running back TreVeyon Henderson, who did not practice Thursday because of illness. Henderson, a second-year second-round pick out of Ohio State, has had a slow start to his 2026 seaosn as the backfield partner to Rhamondre Stevenson, but he did score two touchdowns against Miami in the 2025 season finale. Starting right tackle Morgan Moses (foot) against was limited, while QB Drake Maye was listed with a right shoulder injury, but he was a full participant. The Miami Dolphins look like they're going to be without their top rookie draft pick when they try to upset the New England Patriots on Sunday, but they also might not have to face New England's prized offseason acquisition. Starting with the Dolphins, guard Kadyn Proctor missed a second consecutive practice with a concussion, and it's very difficult to envision him getting clearance to play Sunday. With the Dolphins down to one practice before a walk-through Saturday, it's again difficult to envision Proctor getting clearance in time and also know that the team is going to err on the side of caution here. Head coach Jeff Hafley indicated Wednesday that backup Jarrett Kingston would be taking Proctor's reps at left guard during practice. Kingston was the one who replaced Jonah Savaiinaea at right guard after the 2025 second-round pick was injured in the first half of the Week 5 loss at Hard Rock Stadium. Kingston, who obviously is the No. 3 guard on the roster, was claimed off waivers from the Houston Texans after the cuts to 53. For those wondering about new guard Christian Haynes, claimed off waivers from the Seattle Seahawks on Wednesday, there's basically zero chance he would start that quickly and he actually probably will be inactive for his first game on the Dolphins roster. With the Patriots, the big news involved wide receiver A.J. Brown, who the team acquired in a trade with the Philadelphia Eagles in the offseason. home.blurb: TreVeyon Henderson and A.J. Brown did not participate in Thursday's practice. The running back hadn't been listed as the week began in Foxborough, while the wide receiver had been limited due to a knee issue as well as the high ankle sprain that sent him to injured reserve in September. An illness kept Henderson out of Thursday's practice in Foxborough. The No. 38 overall pick in the 2025 NFL draft stands with 203 rushing yards, 45 receiving yards and one touchdown through 57 touches this fall for the backfield. He saw a season-low three carries during his most recent outing, however. Out wide, since being activated back to the 53-man roster after four games away, Brown has played 101 out of 122 offensive snaps. But the June trade acquisition stands with just six receptions for 75 yards through those recent starts. And now with a knee flare-up coming out of the team's mini bye. The rest of the active roster includes wide receivers DeMario Douglas, Efton Chism III and Kyle Williams. That's with veteran targets Romeo Doubs and Mack Hollins both on injured reserve . Three limited participants remained for head coach Mike Vrabel's side of the AFC East aisle. With one Brown downgraded on Thursday, another Brown went forward in the partial group. New England's starting right guard had been ruled out during the 26-19 win over the New York Jets at Gillette Stadium and was subsequently a non-participant heading into the 30-24 loss to the Chicago Bears at Soldier Field. They sit at 1-4-1 ahead of Sunday's road matchup against the Philadelphia Eagles. Philadelphia is also in a difficult position, sitting at 2-5 while dealing with a plethora of injuries on the offensive side of the ball. Ahead of the matchup, longtime NFL head coach and current Barstool Sports personality Jon Gruden discussed the upcoming NFC East showdown during his weekly "Gruden Family Football Show" with his brother, Jay. Gruden Makes Bold Jayden Daniels Prediction While both teams have some clear question marks, the Commanders have one major advantage in Gruden's eyes: their star quarterback, Jayden Daniels. The Eagles, meanwhile, will be without Jalen Hurts for the rest of the season. Gruden believes Daniels is poised for a huge performance Sunday night and will lead Washington to a much-needed victory. "I expect Jayden Daniels to tear these guys up," Gruden said. "What bothers about Philadelphia is there defense… I don't see nothing. They're going to get smoked by Jayden Daniels and the Washington Commanders. I think this is a get back on track game for the Commanders and anything can happen. The East is still wide open. But Jayden Daniels in the second half against the 49ers , just watch that tape and you'll see this kid winning in the pocket. He can win the pocket. And when the pocket breaks down we know what he can do." Daniels' 2026 Season With the Commanders In his third year with Washington, Daniels has faced some criticism for his in-game decision-making over the past two weeks. However, overall, he's been effective when on the field this season. Through four games, Daniels has completed 64.7% of his passes for 759 yards, five touchdowns and zero interceptions. He's also rushed 25 times for 213 yards and two touchdowns. In three career meetings against the Eagles, Daniels has completed 61.0% of his passes for 613 yards, eight touchdowns and three interceptions. away.headline: Eagles injury report: 6 players DNP for second straight day
away.blurb: Defensively, Philadelphia listed six players as limited participants, including Jonathan Greenard (ankle), Jalyx Hunt (knee/ankle), Nolan Smith (concussion), Moro Ojomo (neck), Michael Carter II (abdomen) and Marcus Epps (jaw/concussion evaluation). Epps was a new addition to the report, while Nolan Smith's continued limited participation represents progress as he works through the concussion protocol. Mondon's improvement from limited participation Wednesday to full participation Thursday was another positive development for a defense dealing with linebacker injuries. This article originally appeared on Eagles Wire: Eagles injury report: 6 players DNP for second straight day The Philadelphia Eagles continue to deal with significant injuries on both sides of the football, with six players missing Thursday's practice ahead of Sunday's NFC East matchup against the Washington Commanders . Running back Saquon Barkley (hamstring/back), wide receivers DeVonta Smith (hamstring), Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) and Britain Covey (knee), linebacker Jihaad Campbell (hamstring/quad) and cornerback Jonathan Jones (hamstring) were all listed as nonparticipants for the second consecutive day. Unlike Wednesday, when Philadelphia held a walkthrough and estimated participation, Thursday's designations followed the team's first full practice of the week. Barkley's continued absence is particularly concerning after he suffered a back injury during Monday night's 38-21 loss to Dallas. The veteran returned from a hamstring injury that previously sidelined him for two games, but he couldn't finish the Cowboys matchup. Philadelphia's backfield is already depleted after the Eagles placed Dameon Pierce on injured reserve Wednesday. Elijah Mitchell and Jaydon Blue are the only other running backs on the active roster, making Barkley's availability critical for an offense struggling to establish consistency. The Eagles are also facing significant questions at wide receiver. Smith and Wicks missed Monday's loss, while Covey exited with a knee injury. Their continued absence could create additional opportunities for rookie Makai Lemon, who caught his first career touchdown against Dallas. The Eagles received encouraging news elsewhere, with Zack Baun, Jakorian Bennett, Landon Dickerson, Arnold Ebiketie, Dallas Goedert, Drew Kendall, Smael Mondon Jr. and Tyler Steen practicing fully. Philadelphia enters Sunday's matchup at 2-5, with five straight losses. The Eagles will release their final injury report Friday, when the status of Barkley, Smith, Wicks, and several defensive contributors should become clearer. Complete Eagles Thursday injury report

I just had a little bit of inflammation in there, had to let that settle down, but felt really good running out there today," Goedert said after Saturday's practice. "I want to be out there anytime I can. We only get 17 games. To miss a game, to miss two games, it always stinks. So if I can be available, I'm going to do everything I can to play. home.headline: Update: Daron Payne tops Commanders trade rumors as Terry McLaurin injury opens a receiver hunt
home.blurb: Receiver became the loudest need the moment McLaurin went down. “Man, he brings a lot on and off the field,” Dan Quinn said, per WJLA . Stefon Diggs caught six passes for 44 yards and a touchdown against the 49ers, but behind him the room is thin, which is why we laid out four ways to replace him the next day. Payne is the name every national board keeps coming back to. The Athletic’s Daniel Popper ranked him 13th on his deadline board and named the Bears and 49ers as fits, an argument we broke down when an NFL analyst said it’s time to sell . A day earlier, Bleacher Report’s Kristopher Knox put him eighth on his trade block big board , with the Bears and Jaguars as suitors and a conditional 2027 fourth-round pick or a veteran receiver as the return. Jayden Daniels threw for 300 yards in San Francisco on Oct. 19, and the Washington Commanders still flew home from a 23-17 loss into the bye at 1-4-1, last in the NFC East. They also lost Terry McLaurin to a torn patellar tendon that night, which leaves Adam Peters with two jobs before the deadline: deciding what to sell and finding a receiver for Daniels. The deadline is 4 p.m. ET on Nov. 10. Washington hosts the Eagles in Landover on Sunday night, Nov. 1, then the Rams on Nov. 8, per the team’s schedule . Unlike most sellers, the Commanders have money to spend. They sit at $25.5 million in cap space, sixth in the league, per Over the Cap . What the Commanders need before the deadline The defense is the bigger problem. Washington allows 28.7 points per game, 31st in the NFL, and 1,524 passing yards through six games, 30th, per Pro Football Reference . The team has only 11 sacks. Odafe Oweh has three of them in the first year of a $100 million deal, and his slow start raises questions about how much help is coming from the edge. Sonny Styles has 46 tackles. Peters told 106.7 The Fan before the 49ers game that the team was making calls but wasn’t giving up on the season, with the division still within reach, per SB Nation’s Scott Bair . Quinn sounded like a coach using the week off to reset. “Sometimes taking a step back can be exactly what you need,” he said, per The Associated Press . Every Commanders trade rumor so far Daron Payne, DT, Commanders (Oct. 22) Sports Illustrated’s Matt Verderame ranked him 10th among 15 players who could be traded on Oct. 20 and paired him with the Lions and 49ers, and PFF’s Bradley Locker had him on his list of 15 candidates back on Oct. 7. Payne has a 65.0 overall grade with 17 pressures and one sack, according to PFF , and he is in the final year of his deal. That is why he’s Washington’s best trade chip , and a trade now brings back a 2027 pick instead of waiting on a compensatory pick in 2028. Andrew Wylie, OL, Commanders (Oct. 22) ESPN’s Bill Barnwell pitched sending Wylie to New England with a 2027 seventh-round pick in exchange for a 2027 sixth. Barkley's status remains one of the biggest concerns after the veteran suffered a back injury during Monday night's 38-21 loss to the Dallas Cowboys. The Eagles listed him with hamstring and back injuries Wednesday, adding another concern for a player who recently returned from a hamstring issue that kept him out of consecutive games. Seattle also won in primetime in Week 7, holding the Kansas City Chiefs to just three points on Sunday Night Football to get back over .500 this season (4-3). These two teams are both in second place in their respective divisions, and this game could have massive wild card implications in the NFC. The NFC North currently has four teams over .500 while the NFC West has two with the 3-4 Los Angeles Rams lurking as a viable Super Bowl contender if they can get healthy. They hit road to play the Super Bowl-champion Seattle Seahawks. And they'll do it with a brand new All-Pro defensive tackle! Jeffery Simmons is a Bear! The Bears are proving themselves to be one of the best offenses in the league with one of the best rising-star quarterbacks. And their head coach and quarterback face a huge test against one of the league's best defenses. Chicago didn't fare so well in their first defensive test of the year, against the Minnesota Vikings. However, the weather was a factor in that game, like it or not. Plus, Caleb Williams didn't finish the game. Excuses, maybe, but also realities. This matchup has a lot of great storylines and will be a measuring stick for the Bears to see how they compete against the league's best. It feels like a game with playoff implications. It feels like a game worthy of the Monday Night Football spotlight. It will be the first game in November for the Bears, too. When teams really start to separate themselves. Let's meet the Seahawks. Seattle Seahawks SB Nation site : Field Gulls Record: 4-3, second in the NFC West Last week: 20-3 win over the Kansas City Chiefs Game day, time, TV: Monday, 7:15 p.m. CT, ESPN Spread: Seattle -3.5 Bears all-time record against: 8-12, including 2-0 postseason Historical meeting: The Bears have never beaten the Seahawks in the month of November. In the second-ever meeting between the teams, the Seahawks beat the Bears 31-29 in week 10 of 1978. The Bears fell behind 21-9 with Jim Zorn hitting Steve Largent twice for touchdowns and Sherman Smith rushing for another. But Chicago made a strong comeback. Roland Harper scored on a 20-yard pass from Mike Phipps. After another Smith touchdown, Walter Payton scored from 7 yards out, drawing the Bears within six. The Seahawks drove down the field and tacked on another field goal to go up 31-22. Phipps threw a pick but Sam McCullum intercepted Zorn right back. Phipps put together a good drive and Harper scored a 2-yard TD with 40 seconds left. The Bears managed to recover the onside kick but with 12 seconds left, from Seattle's 46-yard line, Phipps' pass was intercepted to end the game. Last meeting: Who could forget the awful, terrible 6-3 Thursday Night Football game? Thomas Brown was coaching the Bears. It was a defensive slugfest. Or a total offensive mess. Depends on how you remember it. The most memorable play didn't count, as Caleb Williams rolled out and threw an off-platform pass to Rome Odunze four a touchdown. It was called back for offensive holding. (I cannot find a clip online, but I remember it was awesome). Offense: The Seahawks offense ranks 13th in points and 15th in yards. Their passing offense is 16th and their rushing offense ranks 17th. Sam Darnold (62.1 pct. cmp./1,290 yds./8 TD/8 INT) currently leads the league in interceptions, but played a lot better last week. Unless you've been living under a rock, you likely know about Jaxon Smith-Njigba (58 rec./867 yds./8 TD). Beyond him are AJ Barner (19/180/0), Cooper Kupp (18/199/1), deep threat Rashid Shaheed (16/163/0) and George Holani (12/88/0). Jadarian Price (28 att./119 yds./0 TD) is injured, but expected to return to practice this week along with Zach Charbonnett (no stats in 2026 yet). In their absence, it's been Emanuel Wilson (111 att./403 yds./3 TD) and Holani (26/108/1). Defense: Seattle's defense comes into Monday night as one the league's best. They rank fourth in points allowed and first in yards allowed. Their passing defense ranks first in passing yards and sixth in rushing. The loaded unit stars Nick Emmanwori (27 tkls/3 TFL/2 sk/1 PD/7 QB hits), DTs Leonard Williams (3 sk/7 TFL/9 QB hits/1 PD), Byron Murphy (3 sk/ 24 tkls/5 TFL/6 QB hits) Derick Hall (3 sk/19 QB hits/3 TFL/1 FF/1 FR) and Ernest Jones (3 sk/68 tkls/3 TFL/2 QB hits/1 INT/3 PD) and Devon Witherspoon (41 tkls/3 PD/3 TFL/1 QB hits) Other playmakers are Julian Love (2 INT/6 PD/24 tkls/2 TFL), Nehemiah Pritchett (13 tkls/4 PD/2 INT) and Josh Jobe (27 tkls/1 PD/1 INT/1 TFL). Key matchups: This is a top offense against a top defense. The Bears are going to have to play disciplined football. Take what their given, take shots when they can, use play-action to suck in the LBs. On defense, stop JSN. That's no easy task. The Seahawks can find a running game if Price and/or Charbonnett are back. Anyway to get pressure on Sam Darnold is good though; we know what happens when he is pressured. The Seahawks haven't allowed a 300-yard passer this season. The Rams are the only team with more than 300 passing yards against Seattle since week 2 of last season. Seattle has lost only three times at home going back to the beginning of last season. The 49ers are the only team to beat Seattle at home during this span Despite their strong numbers, the Seahawks have allowed opponents to score on 78.6 percent of their trips inside of the red zone. The Seahawks' 13 offensive turnovers on the season rank fourth-most in the league. Their 12 defensive turnovers rank third-most. Seattle is allowing a league-low 144.4 passing yards per game and the second-worst passer rating of 72.6. Only the Vikings allow a worse QB rating Can the Bears hang with a team as good as the Seahawks? How will their offense and QB measure up against Seattle's defense?

Bears vs. Seahawks bold predictions for Week 8 Monday Night Football Steve Silverman, ClutchPoints Wed, October 28, 2026 at 11:24 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Chicago Bears have demonstrated quite a bit of explosiveness this season, especially when Caleb Williams is under center and running back Kyle Monangai is healthy and in the lineup. Williams has been in the lineup for the past two games and has demonstrated no ill effects from the hamstring injury that sidelined him earlier in the year. Monangai has missed the last three games and while he is improving, there are no guarantees that he will be back in the lineup for this game. The Seahawks have not been at their best in the first half of the season and they take a 4-3 record into this home game. They are coming off a key Sunday night victory over the Kansas City Chiefs in which their defense performed at a peak level. They will need that kind of effort against the Bears. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Sam Darnold was one of the keys to Seattle's surge to last year's Super Bowl title. He has not been as efficient this season, as interceptions have been an issue. The Bears defense got a huge lift from their ability to create takeaways last year. They have not been as proficient in that area this season — minus-1 on the takeaway/turnover table — but they have been a middle-of-the-pack defense that has been moderately capable this season. This game could come down to turnover differential, and if the Bears are going to win on the road, they have to gain an advantage in this area. Williams will throw for 250 yards and 2 TDs Williams has demonstrated that he can rise to the occasion and handle pressure. He has an excellent partnership with head coach Ben Johnson, and it appears that those two will allow the Bears to remain contenders in the division and the NFC for several years. Williams has all the tools that an outstanding quarterback needs, and as the No. 1 selection in the 2024 NFL Draft, nearly all scouts and personnel specialists were predicting great things for him. However, Williams struggled in his rookie season under former head coach Matt Eberflus. That coach did not have the wherewithal to teach and demand outstanding play from Williams. However that changed under Johnson, and the quarterback reads and understands defenses, and he knows how to pick apart good defenses and make key plays. The one area that scouts did not get right about Williams was his speed and escapability from the pocket. He was thought to be above average or good in that area, and that assessment did not give him enough credit. He is sensational in that area. He has a strong partnership with wide receivers Rome Odunze and Luther Burden, as well as big-play tight end Colston Loveland. This trio should be able to cause problems for the Seattle defense, which is one of the strongest units in the league. Williams and the receivers will not overpower the Seahawks defense, but the quarterback will throw 2 TD passes and approach the 275-yard mark. Smith-Njigba is unstoppable, will exceed 125 yards and score a TD Mandatory Credit: Joe Nicholson-Imagn Images The Bears regularly have to contend with outstanding receivers like Justin Jefferson, Amon-Ra St. Brown and Christian Watson in the NFC North. However, Seattle wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba is at another level. He is coming off a sensational game against the Kansas City Chiefs. Smith-Njigba was targeted 12 times by Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold and he caught 9 passes for 150 yards and 1 touchdown. The Chiefs knew he was the central point of the Seattle offensive game plan, yet defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo could not do anything to slow him down. Stopping him was out of the question. Chicago defensive coordinator Dennis Allen will face the same issue. Allen certainly knows what it is like to face outstanding wideouts in the NFC North, but Smith-Njigba may be too strong for the Bears defense. He has caught 58 passes for 867 yards and 8 TDs, and asking CBs Jaylon Johnson, Malik Muhammad and Kyler Gordon to prevent him from making big plays will be folly. The best way for the Bears to go about it would be pressuring Darnold and keep him from delivering accurate passes. The Bears have registered 19 sacks and Darnold has been trapped 14 times thus far. Allen's top priority will be to make sure his personnel gets in Darnold's face and prevents him from getting the ball to Smith-Njigba. That scenario is unlikely, but it is Chicago's best defensive hope. Bold game prediction: Seahawks 27, Bears 24 The Bears have the weapons to go into Seattle and give the defending champions a battle for 60 minutes. This is the kind of game that Johnson and Williams would like to use as a measuring stick. However, the Seahawks have already lost 3 games and they can't afford to lose any more. They will have a major challenge chasing down the 49ers in the NFC West, and dropping a home game to a solid team is not in their plans. The Seahawks played their best all-around game against the Chiefs in Week 7, and they will stay on track against the Bears. Seattle wins a close, well-played game against Williams and the Bears. Among those limited were running back Jadarian Price (chest) who returned to practice from injured reserve this week, and linebackers Drake Thomas (ankle) and Chazz Surratt (calf), who have both missed multiple games with injuries. New to the injury report this week is defensive tackle Leonard Williams , who was limited with an Achilles injury. The Bears did not practice Thursday, so their report is an estimation, but running back Kyle Monangai was listed as a non-participant due to thumb and toe injuries, while linebacker D'Marco Jackson (ankle) and cornerback Malik Muhammad (toe) were listed as limited. news Ty Okada Out, Nick Emmanwori Questionable For Seahawks' Season Opener vs. Patriots Week 8 Injury Report: Bears at Seahawks Skip to main content Primary nav NEWS Presented by Week 8 Injury Report: Bears at Seahawks Details on the Seahawks’ injury situation heading into their Week 8 game vs. the Bears. John Boyle Seahawks.com Senior Reporter The Seahawks' first injury report of the week had four players listed as non-participants due to injury, including three who left last weekend's win over the Chiefs with injuries: left tackle Charles Cross (ankle), receiver Rashid Shaheed (knee) and running back Velus Jones Jr. (hamstring). Also not participating were linebacker Uchenna Nwosu , who has an ankle injury, and receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba , who was given a rest day. home.headline: Bears Catch a Huge Break on Seahawks Week 8 Injury Report
home.blurb: Veteran tackle Josh Jones, who started three games for Seattle last season, is expected to take over the starting job for however long he'll be out of the lineup. With 27 career starts, Jones has seen a lot of action throughout his career. He's a backup for a reason, though. With the Bears playing on Thursday night, they have a three-day rest advantage over the Seahawks. Their mini-Bye Week could allow them to get T.J. Edwards back in the lineup. Montez Sweat will also return from a two-game suspension for violating the league's substance abuse policy. Meanwhile, they've also gotten quality production from Daniel Hardy after he's filled in for Sweat over the past two weeks. He has one-and-a-half sacks and eight pressures ( according to PFF ), and might've carved out a role in the rotation until further notice . home.blurb: Bears’ Kyle Monangai Week 8 injury update teases much-needed MNF return vs. Seahawks - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL WNBA Finals: Dream force Game 7 Jackson Stone, ClutchPoints Wed, October 28, 2026 at 6:26 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Chicago Bears are currently gearing up for a big Monday Night Football matchup against the Seattle Seahawks on the road. The Bears will be coming off a long week in this one, having last played last Thursday night in a home win over the New England Patriots. On Wednesday, the Bears got a big update on a key member of their offensive backfield ahead of that matchup. "Bears running back Kyle Monangai (turf toe) has missed the past three weeks, but his chances are better of playing this week," reported NFL insider Jeremy Fowler of ESPN. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) In Monangai's absence, D'Andre Swift has been left to do a lot of the heavy lifting in the running game for the Bears, but having him back should help more evenly distribute the workload for head coach Ben Johnson. Meanwhile, quarterback Caleb Williams has picked up right where he left off since returning from an injury of his own, eviscerating the Atlanta Falcons and the Patriots en route to two straight comfortable wins to improve the Bears' record to 5-2 on the season, and second place in the NFC North behind only the Minnesota Vikings, who remain the last undefeated team in the NFL this year. The running game was a huge part of the Bears' success a year ago, so having Monangai back for Sunday's game against a Seahawks team that just completely shut down the Kansas City Chiefs will be a big boost for Chicago. In any case, kickoff between the Bears and Seahawks is set for Monday evening at 8:15 pm ET from Seattle. home.headline: Seahawks Give New Zach Charbonnet Injury Update Before Bears Game
home.blurb: The Seattle Seahawks are getting closer to Zach Charbonnet's return, but head coach Mike Macdonald isn't ready to put a date on it. "He had a great week, great spirits," Macdonald said. "We have to remember, it's going to be nine months out of ACL surgery. How many people have ever done that? What's it like, Adrian Peterson?" Macdonald wasn't predicting a similar season for Charbonnet. Rather, his comments underscored the significance of attempting to return from major knee surgery on such an accelerated timeline. The roster move made him eligible to play, but Macdonald has repeatedly emphasized that his return will depend on the team's recovery plan. Charbonnet's eventual return would give Seattle another proven rushing option, particularly near the goal line. His absence has been especially noticeable with Kenneth Walker III now playing for the Chiefs and rookie Jadarian Price sidelined. Rookie Jadarian Price is expected to return to practice this week after missing multiple games with a chest injury. However, the Seahawks are sticking with their established recovery plan rather than rushing the running back onto the field. "I'll just say we're sticking to our plan," Macdonald said. "He's still going to practice in a full capacity, and then we'll evaluate it as the week goes on." The update follows Charbonnet's absence from Seattle's 20-3 victory over the Kansas City Chiefs on October 25, despite the 25-year-old participating fully in practice throughout the previous week. Mike Macdonald Invokes Adrian Peterson While Discussing Zach Charbonnet's Recovery Macdonald also put Charbonnet's recovery into perspective, comparing the timeline to one of the NFL's most famous ACL comebacks. Peterson famously returned for the Minnesota Vikings ' 2012 season less than nine months after suffering a torn ACL and MCL in December 2011. He went on to rush for 2,097 yards and win NFL MVP honors. Charbonnet suffered his ACL injury during Seattle's January 17 playoff victory over the San Francisco 49ers and underwent surgery in February.
